The word *subhan* (سُبْحَانَ) means the absolute transcendence (*tanzih*, declaring God free from any imperfection or deficiency) of the Necessary Existent (*wajib al-wujud*) above being governed by the laws of the existent itself. For this reason it is said at every wondrous matter, as in the story of the Night Journey and the Ascension (*al-Isra' wa'l-Mi'raj*).

For this reason you find that this word, *subhan*, is not said, and has never been said before, except of Allah, the Exalted. Despite the number of tyrants on earth, and despite the presence of those who claimed divinity and who said, "I am your Lord, the Most High" (﴿I am your most high lord﴾), it was never said except of Allah. Therefore we say in the remembrance of Allah, "Subhanaka" (Glory be to You), and it is not said except to You. Why? Because it signifies absolute transcendence, and this belongs to Allah alone.

The word *subhan* (كلمة سُبْحَانَ) is a verbal noun (*masdar*). Saying "Subhana Allah" means: transcendence belongs to Allah before there exists anyone who declares Him transcendent. He is transcendent in His essence before anyone says "Subhan Allah," just as He is the Creator before He creates, and the Provider before He provides anyone. The attribute exists in Him, glorified is He, before its object (*muta'allaq*) comes into being. Just as you say of a person, "So-and-so is a poet." Is he a poet because he recited a splendid qasida, or is he a poet before he recited it? Indeed he is a poet before he recites the qasida, and were it not for the gift of poetry in him, he would not have composed it.

Thus, all the attributes of perfection exist in Allah, the Exalted, before their objects come into being, because these attributes are what brought their objects into existence.

Absolute transcendence of the Truth, glorified is He, has three levels:

The first: that you declare His essence transcendent above all essences.

The second: that you declare His attributes transcendent above all (created) attributes. You are described as rich (*ghina*), but your richness is not like the richness of the Truth, glorified is He. You exist and Allah exists; is your existence like His existence, glorified is He?... and so on.

Then the third: that you declare His action transcendent above resembling human actions. When it is said, "Allah did such-and-such," beware of measuring His action by your action. For this reason we said regarding ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra': 1]: measure it by the might of the One who acts, glorified is He, not by your own might.

When the Truth, glorified is He, brings something that the first addressees already know, He does not close the treasuries of His bounty. Rather, He leaves us a reserve for everything that will be discovered afterward as a result of development and pairing, in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36]. So His saying, "and of what they do not know" (وَمِمَّا لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ).

It is unknown to the addressees at first, but it will be known later. The most prominent Qur'anic verse that points to this matter is His saying:

﴿And horses, mules, and donkeys, for you to ride and for adornment; and He creates what you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 8].

So His saying, ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 8], came as a reserve for what was later renewed of means of transport and communication, such as cars, airplanes, rockets, etc.

If you say: why did these newly emerged things come in general terms? We say: because the human mind was not prepared to accept them at the time of the address, since it had seen none of this. But when the thing exists, one sees it plainly. So He, glorified is He, spoke in general terms: ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 8], because every day will bring us something new and wonders we have not seen before. The latest of what we have witnessed of this is rockets, and who knows, perhaps we will soon see something more wondrous than them. At that time we will include all these things under ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 8]...

The Truth, glorified is He, in His saying ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36], only assures us of the continuity of the blessing and of the continuity of the One who bestows it upon us. By pairing, the species remains and multiplies, and duality exists in everything...

Duality exists in everything in existence, as He, glorified is He, said in another verse: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 49].

If you look at this whole existence with the penetrating, experimental, scrutinizing eye of knowledge, you will find that everything in existence is two-fold, for the continuity of its kind...

The Truth, glorified is He, mentioned pairing in ﴿of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36] but did not mention animals. Why? Because He mentioned the higher, which is man, the rational animal, and the rest are like him and follow him.

The meaning of ﴿and of what they do not know﴾ (وَمِمَّا لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ) is that in the universe there are many things whose pairing we do not know, and we may come to know them in the future with the advance of experimental sciences, as happened, for example, with electricity, when we learned that it has a negative and a positive pole, and we do not benefit from electricity unless the negative meets the positive. But if a negative meets a negative, or a positive meets a positive, the result is reversed. The negative and the positive here are a kind of pairing. Likewise is the case with the atom and other things that modern science has discovered.

Thus, the phrase ﴿and of what they do not know﴾ (وَمِمَّا لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ) has meanings that have come to pass. Allah informed us of them before we discovered them, so that we would know that the unseen which Allah informs us of comes as a prelude to another unseen which we will know in the future. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, draws our attention: just as reality has confirmed what I told you of the unseen, so believe what I have told you of the unseen of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 36, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a sign for them is the night﴾. That is, specifically for them, and it is not a sign for everyone; for the Prophet (ﷺ) believed by his natural disposition (fitrah), and had no need of proof in order to believe. Likewise, the believer does not seek proof except to answer with it those who deny...

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿We strip from it the day﴾. Salkh (stripping) is the removing of the skin from a sheep. What is the connection between this matter and the light of night and day? They said: The original state of a thing is darkness, and darkness does not appear except by an incoming light. So night is darkness, then the light of day comes and covers this darkness, as though the day, when it comes, covers the darkness just as the skin of a sheep covers its flesh. So when the Truth, glorified is He, wills that darkness should come, He strips off the light, just as we strip the skin of a sheep from its flesh.

So: the night comes according to its nature, because it is the original state; therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness﴾. Darkness is the absence of light, whereas light is a bringing-into-being, and it requires a new instrument. If the night were left to its own state, it would remain dark, and were it not for the instrument of light, it would remain night. Thus light has an instrument, whereas darkness has no instrument which, when it operates, brings darkness; or, say, the matter of darkness is privative (ʿadamī), whereas the matter of light is existential (wujūdī). So when it is said ﴿We strip from it the day﴾, the light that covers the darkness has been likened to the skin that covers the flesh of the sheep.

The meaning: We remove this luminous covering that conceals the night, so darkness settles in, that is, it appears in its natural state and of its own accord. This is why the Qur'anic expression came with ﴿idhā﴾, which denotes suddenness: ﴿behold, they are in darkness﴾. It is as though the matter is spontaneous, requiring no arrangement.

**Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 36, verse 38:**

The sun is the instrument of the light that We strip from the night. The meaning of ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾ is: for something, and for an end, at which it comes to rest...

So the meaning of ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾ is that the sun, together with its system and the planets that revolve around it, runs toward a star that astronomers call Vega (al-Figa), and that the Arabs call al-Nasr al-Waqi' (the Swooping Eagle)... As for the meaning of ﴿a resting place for it﴾, the resting place is either the end of the year, after which it begins a new year and rises from its first point of rising, or the resting place is the last of its lifespan and its end, when it is folded up, wound up, and brought to an end.

But what moves this solar system? And how does it move at this speed? We know that motion needs energy to sustain it, so what is the energy that moves this system in this manner and with this continuity? They said: it runs because Allah created it in the form of motion and running, so it runs and nothing stops it, and it will continue running until Allah wills otherwise. Therefore it needs no energy to move it. An example of this is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease, and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ [Fatir: 41].

In the science of motion there is a law called the law of inertia (qanun al-'atala), which states that every moving body continues in its motion until something stops it, and every body at rest continues in its rest until something sets it in motion. This law has explained to us the motion of artificial satellites and spacecraft, which remain in motion for long periods.

We ask: for what period do they move throughout this duration? They move because they were placed in their orbit in the form of motion, so they remain in motion, and nothing stops them, because they are beyond the field of gravity (majal al-jadhdhaba). Thus, all the energy these machines needed is the energy of the rocket that carries them, until it takes them beyond the field of Earth's gravity; after that they keep circling without energy and without fuel.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, reminds us of His favour in this motion, saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾. That is, what has preceded of the motion of the night and day and the running of the sun is by the decree of Allah. The word al-'Aziz (the Almighty) here is wholly fitting: the meaning is that He, exalted is He, is the Almighty whom no laws can overpower, because He, glorified is He, is the Creator of the laws.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 36, verse 39:

After the Truth, glorified is He, spoke of the sun, which is the instrument of light, He spoke of the moon, because it has a task it performs when the sun sets. It is as if the moon borrowed some of the sun's light so as to give light at night to those who work only at night, such as the night watchmen (al-'Assas), guards, security men, bakery workers and others. The moon, as you know, does not shine by itself; it only reflects some of the sun's light, so its light comes gentle and calm. For this reason they call it "the gentle light" (al-Diya' al-Halim), since it reaches us with no ray of its own and no heat in it.

Therefore, when the Truth, glorified is He, enumerates some of His signs and blessings, He says: ﴿And of His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty.﴾ [al-Rum: 23].

So if sleep were confined to the night, what would those whose nature of work requires them to work at night, and to rest and sleep by day, be doing? This verse is thus a manifestation of the precision of the Qur'anic expression. If the night is the original time of sleep and rest for the majority of people, there is no objection to sleeping by day for the minority who are charged with the affairs of those who sleep at night.

As for the meaning of: ﴿And We have determined for it phases [manazil]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 39], it means: We have determined its course through phases and stages. These phases we witness every month in the movement of the moon: the first quarter, the second quarter, then the full moon.

The moon is swifter in its movement than the sun, because it completes its orbit in a month, while the sun completes its orbit in a year.

And consider the precision of the Qur'anic expression, founded on the highest geometry, in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿until it returns like the old dried palm-stalk [al-'Urjun al-Qadim]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 39]. This is an illustrative image of the phases of the moon drawn from the Arab environment. Al-'Urjun is the cluster (adhq) of the palm tree that bears the dates, which we call (al-Subatah). It is composed of several thin strands (shamarikh), but its base, where it joins the palm trunk, is broad and flattened. This cluster dries and shrivels as it ages, and it bends and (yatafaqqa') as its moisture dries out. This image wholly clarifies the movement of the moon, for it shrinks and curls until it vanishes at the end of the month.

If the Qur'an has likened the moon to the old palm-stalk, the Arabs liken it to the paring of a fingernail, as in the words of their poet who kept watching the moonlight until it set, so that he could slip away to his beloved:

And the light of the little moon, which I was watching, set, like a paring cut from a fingernail.

It is wise to liken the lofty moon, which we cannot reach, to a near thing that we can reach, and to say to you: this is like that, so that the picture becomes clear.

Then He, glorified is He, says, joining the sun and the moon, and the night and the day:

﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night overtake the day...﴾.

The commentary says: It is not said: "So-and-so cannot overtake so-and-so unless he is behind him." Likewise the sun cannot overtake the moon, because, as we have said, the moon precedes it and is faster than it, since it completes its orbit in a month, while the sun completes its orbit in a year...

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And each in an orbit they swim﴾. "Yasbahun" (they swim) derives from "al-sabh" (swimming), which is covering a distance over soft water. Thus it is a motion with a gliding quality, not upon ground on which feet tread. This is an example of the motion of the celestial orbits, and in this swimming motion every part of it is distributed over a part of time.

We do not have the measures by which we perceive this motion; rather, we know it from the whole of time together with the whole of the motion. For example, if a child is born to you and you sit watching him and observing his growth, you do not notice this growth, and the child never seems to grow in the eyes of his father. Why?

Because his growth does not come in one leap that can be observed; rather, growth is distributed over time. But if you are away from your child for several months or years, you notice his growth when you return and see him, because you notice the total growth over the period of your absence from him.

So the meaning of ﴿And each in an orbit they swim﴾ is: they move with a smooth, continuous motion distributed over time.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 36, verse 41:

His words, Exalted is He, "And a sign for them": it is a sign for us and for them. For us, by way of inference (istidlal), we infer from it and use it to convince them. For them, namely: it calls them to faith in God...

The meaning of al-Fulk is the ships; al-Mashhun is the filled-up (laden). What is meant is the ship of our master Noah, peace be upon him. God revealed to him that he should build the ship, and guided him to the manner of its construction, as He, Glory be to Him, said:

﴿So We revealed to him: "Build the ship under Our eyes and Our inspiration..."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 27].

So ships in themselves are among the signs of God. Had God not inspired Noah to build the ship, how would we travel upon the water, which is three-quarters of the surface of the globe? This is a sign which God brought about through the hand of our master Noah, so that all people would learn the building of ships, and then so that minds could develop them and advance their construction afterwards, as we now see giant ships of the most modern kind, where man has replaced the ship's sail with steam and electrical engines, and iron and metals have taken the place of wood and nails, etc.

Despite this development, and after dispensing with the power of the wind in propelling ships, ships still move by the name of God and by His power, even if they use steam or electricity; for "wind" does not refer only to the air that propels ships, but wind means power, whatever it may be. Therefore He, Glory be to Him, says:

﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength (rih) depart﴾ [al-Anfal: 46].

And He, Glory be to Him, says: ﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface﴾ [al-Shura: 33].

What halts us in this verse is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾. The verse speaks of the Arabs to whom the Qur'an was addressed, and those who were carried in the ship were their fathers, not their descendants. How is that?

The Qur'an says: "We carried their offspring" (dhurriyyatahum), and what is meant is their fathers, because the word dhurriyya is also applied to the father, since the descendants (dharari) come from him; or because the fathers who were saved in the ship are the original root of those present whom the Qur'an addresses, and they were hidden within their fathers.

For this reason we have said before: each one of us, until the Hour arises, has within him a living cell from his father Adam which has not been touched by death. If you were to trace the fathers and follow this chain, you would say: I am from a living microbe that came from my father, and my father is from a living microbe that came from his father, and so on back to Adam, peace be upon him; and had this microbe been dead, I would not have come into being.

So, then: in each of us there is a constitutive particle from our father Adam which has not undergone any change, and this particle is what carries the natural faith (fitra al-imaniyya) in every human being.

The Truth, Glory be to Him, described the ship as "laden," meaning filled-up; because our master Noah did not take the believers aboard merely to save them from drowning, but to provide them with the means of livelihood after deliverance. Otherwise, how would people live on a land in which there was no one else, no plants, no animals, no birds?

For this reason He, Glory be to Him, said, addressing His Prophet Noah: ﴿We said: "Carry in it of every kind two, a pair"﴾ [Hud: 40].

For us, it serves as evidence (istidlal, reasoning from a sign to what it indicates), by which we argue to convince them. For them, it calls them to faith in God. For this reason, when Imam ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, was asked, "Did you know your Lord through Muhammad, or did you know Muhammad through your Lord?" he replied: "I knew my Lord through my Lord, and Muhammad came and conveyed to me what my Lord intended for me."

Otherwise, how would people live on a land in which there was no one else, no plants, no animals, and no birds?

For this reason He, glorified is He, said to His prophet Noah: ﴿We said, "Carry in it of every kind two pairs..."﴾ [Hud: 40].

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And We created for them of the like of it that they ride﴾ [Ya-Sin: 42]: after the ship, people took it as a model, built its likeness, and developed its construction, and so they produced ships, vessels, boats, and other things ridden upon the sea. Or: We created for them of its like what they ride in the wilderness and the desert; and from this they call the camel, by way of illustration, "the ship of the desert."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, warns us not to be deceived by these vessels, because they are only means of salvation. He, glorified is He, if He wills destruction, destroys. How often have we seen gigantic vessels equipped with every means of safety and security, yet the waves swallowed them with all who were aboard.

God has spoken truly: ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no one to cry out for them, nor are they rescued﴾ [Ya-Sin: 43]. So beware, when you are granted a blessing that saves you from peril, lest the blessing deceive you into thinking that safety and deliverance lie in it. For you will not escape the grip of God, and no one can rescue you, and nothing can save you if He wills your destruction. Do you see in your hand anything that could save you when a storm blows, or when the waves rise over your ship like mountains? Therefore, your devices and means do not save you from My decree.

The meaning of ﴿there is no one to cry out for them﴾ [Ya-Sin: 43]: the "sarikh" is the one you call upon for help and seek aid from, so that he rescues you, takes you by the hand, and brings you out of the predicament you are in. Among the marvellous beliefs that the people of illumination and enlightenment (ahl al-ishraq wa'l-tanwir) have discerned is their saying: a person cries out and seeks rescue from the one nearest to him, such as his father, or his mother, or his servant, or his neighbour, and so on. If he finds none, he says: "O Allah." For this reason we hear some of them say in a predicament: "Ya Huwah." What is meant by "Ya Huwa" is "O Allah," because there is no other who rescues and relieves.

The meaning of ﴿and as enjoyment for a time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 44] is that this deliverance is not a guarantee of lasting safety and continuous survival; rather, it is an enjoyment for a time, until the appointed term arrives and death overtakes you. So you have been spared from one destruction only to face the destruction that is unavoidable.

Similar to this is the saying of al-Fakhr al-Razi:

Had we, when we die, found rest, then death would be the repose of every living being.
But when we die we are raised again, and after that we are questioned about everything.

Rather, this deliverance is an enjoyment for a time, until the appointed term arrives and death overtakes you. Thus you have been saved from one fate (al-ḥimām) only to meet the fate that is unavoidable (al-ḥimām alladhī lā budda minh).

...the meaning of "lahum" (to them) is: to the disbelievers. The verb "qila" (it is said) is used here in the passive form to convey generality, as if every believer is obligated to say it, to advise, and to take the hand of others onto the path of Allah.

In this verse, the Exalted says to His believing servants: "O My servants, O you who have believed in Me and affirmed My messengers, I wish that you would not spare any effort to save My creation from My anger upon them, when they persist in disbelief and remain upon it."

This is a kind of hope placed in the believers, that they take the hand of the disbelievers, and rescue them from the causes of Allah's anger upon them. This meaning falls under the saying of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself."

The meaning of "ma bayna aydikum" (what is before you) is: what is in front of you, and what awaits you of resurrection, gathering, questioning and reckoning, then the Fire. "Wa ma khalfakum" (and what is behind you) [Ya-Sin: 45] means: what preceded you of lessons from those who denied before you, and how their end was and the outcome of their disbelief. "La'allakum turhamun" (so that you may be shown mercy) means: in hope that Allah will have mercy upon you.

Therefore: it is fitting that the believer have in mind to pave the way for the mercy of the disbeliever, to strive with his utmost effort to save him, and to show him compassion, not to adopt with him the course of contention and enmity, which is of no benefit.

This is pure obstinacy and stubbornness. The signs are plain before them, yet they turn away from them and refuse to reflect upon them. That is because those who disbelieve in God and reject His messengers, and who scorn the method of God that came to safeguard His vicegerent on earth, are people who profit from corruption and profit from turning away from God's method. Naturally, they see in every messenger and in every reformer one who has come to cut off their livelihoods and spoil their lives, so they confront him and stand against him.

This verse is explained by God's words in another place: ﴿And they denied them wrongfully and arrogantly, though their souls were convinced of them﴾ [An-Naml: 14].

If you say: since you are eager for God to have mercy on these disbelievers, why do you not press them with new signs until they believe and God has mercy on them? We say: however much signs we bring them, we will arrive at this conclusion which the Qur'an has established: ﴿And no sign comes to them from among the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾ [Ya-Sin: 46].

This is another form of their obstinacy and their inversion of realities. When the sincere adviser says to them, "Spend of what God has provided you" (أَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ الله), meaning: of what He has made you vicegerents over, not of what you own, and what He has made His possession and given to you, their reply is, "Shall we feed one whom God, if He willed, would have fed?" "Shall we feed one whom God, if He willed, would have fed" (أَنُطْعِمُ مَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ اللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُ): meaning, we are not stingy; rather we love to spend and to carry out God's purposes in His creation. But God wills to withhold provision from these people, so how should we provide for them? If we spent on them, we would be obstinate and opposing God's will. "If God willed, He would have fed them."

Their obstinacy does not stop at this limit; rather they go further and accuse the believers of "clear error" (إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلاَّ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ), meaning: "You are only in clear error." Glory be to God! Why? Because you oppose God's will, and you feed those whom God has deprived, and you act as a protector for them.

Yes, the Truth, glorified is He, is the Lord of all, and He provides for all, and feeds us and gives us drink. But He, glorified is He, wills that the compassion of His servants toward one another be manifest, so that their movement in life proceeds without rancor and without spite. The poor man, when he receives some good from the rich man, does not harbor resentment or envy toward him, but rather wishes the blessing to endure for him. Moreover, wealth and poverty are an accident that passes and ceases, and reality bears witness to this.

Their saying, "When will this promise be fulfilled?" ﴿مَتَىٰ هَذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ﴾ [Ya-Sin: 48] — that is, the promise of the Hereafter. The word "promise" (al-wa'd) indicates good tidings, unlike the threat (al-wa'id), which is a warning of evil. So it is strange of them to deny a promise when it is in their favour, and their share lies in the promise, not in the threat.

This question from them is posed in the manner of denial: there is no Hereafter, no reckoning, and no recompense. The sensible among them who acknowledges the Hereafter would say what the owner of the garden said: ﴿وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَائِمَةً وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي لأَجِدَنَّ خَيْراً مِّنْهَا مُنْقَلَباً﴾ [Al-Kahf: 36].

The meaning of ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ [Ya-Sin: 48] — "if you are truthful" — is in your claim that there is a resurrection and a reckoning. The defiance, obstinacy and haste for the Resurrection in their denial of it is clear. They say: "Where is this Resurrection you speak of? Bring it now, if you are truthful." And one of them remains in this argument until the Resurrection surprises him.

This is a warning to the heedless, who were unmindful of the resurrection, the gathering and the reckoning, and whom the world occupied with their trade, their farming and the troubles of their lives, until they squandered their lives in give-and-take, argument and quarrel, until the Resurrection surprised them. Therefore the poet says: "Beware of disputing over a thing that was in your hand, for another has taken it from you":

My soul, which possesses all things, is departing;
so how should I grieve over a thing whose gold is hers?

The meaning of ﴿تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin: 49] — it surprises them while they are in their dispute and quarrel. The meaning of ﴿يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin: 49] is "they dispute" (yakhtasimun); the taa' was changed to a saad and merged into the saad, to indicate intensity. And seizing (al-akhdh) indicates severity: ﴿أَخْذَ عِزِيزٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ﴾ [Al-Qamar: 42] — "the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent."

His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً﴾ [Ya-Sin: 50] — meaning: the blast and the Resurrection surprise them, so that no one is able to make a bequest to anyone. The bequest (al-wasiyya) is well known: a person enjoins upon his family and children what is important in their lives. Thus we have seen that the Master of Messengers, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he sensed the approach of his appointed time during the Farewell Pilgrimage, gave counsel to the Muslims in his comprehensive sermon, which contains the essence of the religion and its foundations. Likewise, whoever faces his term and senses its end should enjoin upon those he cares for the important matters.

So then: in this situation there is no time left for them to counsel one another ﴿وَلاَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin: 50] — "nor do they return to their families." And the Trumpet will be blown, and behold, from the graves they will rush forth to their Lord. (Ya-Sin 36:51)

That is, the trumpet which Israfil will blow. This is the blast of resurrection, and it will be preceded by the blast of swooning (al-Sa'q), which causes them to die and become senseless. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.﴾ (al-Zumar 39:68)

If you say: the blast is one, so how can it cause the first to die and the second to revive? We say: the blowing into the Trumpet is nothing but a sign of the event; the true Doer is Allah, glorified and exalted is He. It is He who causes death at the first and gives life at the second.

The meaning of al-Ajdath (ﷺ, the graves) is the tombs. ﴿To their Lord they will rush﴾ means: they will hasten. The root of the word yansiluna (they rush) is from "nasala" (to slip out), as threads slip out of one another. We say: the garment "yansilu," meaning some of its threads come out of their places from the weft or the warp. Therefore we say: "kaff" (stitch) the sewing, meaning: prevent this "tanseel" by holding the threads together to one another, so that they do not slip loose.

When they come out of the graves and see the reality that they used to deny, they say: ﴿O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:52) It is they who say this and call down woe upon themselves; no one says to them "woe to you"; it is they who say it to themselves, and this is an expression of the regret over what they have missed.

The meaning: "O woe to us, appear, for this is your time, because the matter is beyond what we can bear, and we cannot repel it." When a person is confronted with the corruption of his opinion, he turns to blame himself, and may even strike and punish himself.

It is strange of them that they now say, ﴿Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?﴾ thereby acknowledging that death was merely a sleeping place, and a sleeper must inevitably wake. Then it will be answered them: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke truly.﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:52) That is: what you see of the matters of the Resurrection. It is also permissible that the demonstrative ﴿this﴾ refers to ﴿our sleeping place﴾ in ﴿Who has raised us up from our sleeping place this?﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted, informed that He will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, and that whoever escapes the punishments of the world and the torment of the life in which they live, then Allah has stored up for him a torment of a more severe kind. For those who stood up to call to Allah at the beginning, and were persecuted and harmed, some of them died under persecution before they saw the victory of Islam and the triumph of the Muslims, and before they saw Allah's vengeance upon His enemies. If this is the case, then Allah must show these believers the outcome of the disbelievers and the punishment that befell them.

The promise here, although it is a warning of the evil awaiting them, is called in their regard a promise and not a threat. Why? Because warning of evil before it befalls is a great blessing, as in the words of Allah, exalted is He, in Surat al-Rahman: ﴿There will be sent upon you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be able to defend yourselves. So which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ (al-Rahman 55:35-36)

He made the fire and the flame among the blessings of Allah, because He frightens them with it and warns them of it, and does not surprise them with it while they are healthy, hearing and seeing, and able to return to Allah and repent to Him; they are in a time of respite and remedy. Just as you warn your son of failing if he neglects his lessons and threaten him, so the threat here is itself a blessing; therefore it is called a promise and not a threat.

As for the meaning of ﴿and the messengers spoke truly﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:52): that is, in conveying the message from Allah. ﴿It will be but one shout﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:53): that is, the blast will not be: ﴿but a single shout﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:53), not repeated; because what repeats an action is man, and its repetition means that the first action was not sufficient and did not fulfil its purpose. But here the Doer is Allah, mighty and majestic.

﴿It will be but one shout, and behold, they will all be brought before Us (Ya-Sin 36:53).﴾ "Idha" here is sudden (fujaʼiyya), so by the mere shout they are all brought forth against their will and without their choice. "Muhdar" is the passive participle of "ahdara" (to bring forth): that is, they are compelled to appear and stand before Allah for reckoning.

In the preceding verse, ﴿And all of them, when they are gathered, will be brought before Us (Ya-Sin 36:32)﴾, the word "kull" (all) was added, indicating the inclusion of individuals. Inclusion of individuals may come in succession, one group after another, but here they come all together, so that the follower may see the one he followed, and the misguided may see the one who misled him, etc.; therefore they call it "al-Fadiha" (the Exposing).

Therefore we say: "kaff" (stitch) the sewing, meaning: prevent this "tanseel" by holding the threads together to one another, so that they do not slip loose.

When they come out of the graves and see the reality that they used to deny, they say: ﴿O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:52) It is they who say this and call down woe upon themselves; no one says to them "woe to you"; it is they who say it to themselves, and this is an expression of the regret over what they have missed.

The meaning: "O woe to us, appear, for this is your time, because the matter is beyond what we can bear, and we cannot repel it." When a person is confronted with the corruption of his opinion, he turns to blame himself, and may even strike and punish himself.

It is strange of them that they now say, ﴿Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?﴾ thereby acknowledging that death was merely a sleeping place, and a sleeper must inevitably wake. Then it will be answered them: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke truly.﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:52) That is: what you see of the matters of the Resurrection. It is also permissible that the demonstrative ﴿this﴾ refers to ﴿our sleeping place﴾ in ﴿Who has raised us up from our sleeping place this?﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted, informed that He will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, and that whoever escapes the punishments of the world and the torment of the life in which they live, then Allah has stored up for him a torment of a more severe kind. For those who stood up to call to Allah at the beginning, and were persecuted and harmed, some of them died under persecution before they saw the victory of Islam and the triumph of the Muslims, and before they saw Allah's vengeance upon His enemies. If this is the case, then Allah must show these believers the outcome of the disbelievers and the punishment that befell them.

The promise here, although it is a warning of the evil awaiting them, is called in their regard a promise and not a threat. Why? Because warning of evil before it befalls is a great blessing, as in the words of Allah, exalted is He, in Surat al-Rahman: ﴿There will be sent upon you both a flame of fire and smoke, and you will not be able to defend yourselves. So which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ (al-Rahman 55:35-36)

He made the fire and the flame among the blessings of Allah, because He frightens them with it and warns them of it, and does not surprise them with it while they are healthy, hearing and seeing, and able to return to Allah and repent to Him; they are in a time of respite and remedy. Just as you warn your son of failing if he neglects his lessons and threaten him, so the threat here is itself a blessing; therefore it is called a promise and not a threat.

As for the meaning of ﴿and the messengers spoke truly﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:52): that is, in conveying the message from Allah. ﴿It will be but one shout﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:53): that is, the blast will not be: ﴿but a single shout﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:53), not repeated; because what repeats an action is man, and its repetition means that the first action was not sufficient and did not fulfil its purpose. But here the Doer is Allah, mighty and majestic.

﴿It will be but one shout, and behold, they will all be brought before Us (Ya-Sin 36:53).﴾ "Idha" here is sudden (fujaʼiyya), so by the mere shout they are all brought forth against their will and without their choice. "Muhdar" is the passive participle of "ahdara" (to bring forth): that is, they are compelled to appear and stand before Allah for reckoning.

In the preceding verse, ﴿And all of them, when they are gathered, will be brought before Us (Ya-Sin 36:32)﴾, the word "kull" (all) was added, indicating the inclusion of individuals. Inclusion of individuals may come in succession, one group after another, but here they come all together, so that the follower may see the one he followed, and the misguided may see the one who misled him, etc.; therefore they call it "al-Fadiha" (the Exposing).

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, is reassuring the people of faith and righteous deeds, meaning: do not fear the terror of the Resurrection, for We do not wrong anyone, and the recompense with Us is of the same kind as the deed: ﴿And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾. So this verse is a reassurance for whoever has done righteous deeds, and a warning for whoever has done evil deeds.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 36, verse 55:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the companions of the Garden﴾. The companion (ṣāḥib) is the chosen and selected one from your kind, so that you may keep company with him and not part from him. It is as if the Garden were presented in the manner of rational beings who keep company and are kept company. This is because the Garden was in their minds and in their thoughts; they are attached to it, and it is their preoccupation. So they have companionship with the Garden, and the Garden has companionship with them. Whenever they embark upon some good, they remember the Garden and desire it; and whenever they embark upon some evil, they remember the Fire and turn away from it. Or: the companion (ṣāḥib) is the owner of a thing, so it is as if the Garden were their possession; they have possessed it and obtained its keys by what they had sent forward of righteous deeds.

And the meaning of ﴿today﴾ is: that is, the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Occupied in busyness﴾ means: in bliss that occupies them from any other thing. Or: ﴿occupied in busyness﴾ means: occupied away from their acquaintances and relatives who entered the Fire, may God protect us, as He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And fear a day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all﴾ [Luqman: 33]. So they are in a bliss that occupies them from all of these, as though they do not recognize them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 36, verse 56:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Indeed, the companions of the Garden﴾ [Ya-Sin: 55]. The companion (al-sahib) is the one chosen and selected from your own kind, so that you may keep company with him and not part from him. It is as though the Garden has been presented in the manner of rational beings who keep company and are kept company. This is because the Garden was in their minds and in their thoughts; they are attached to it, and it is their preoccupation. So they have a companionship with the Garden, and the Garden has a companionship with them. Whenever they proceed toward good, they remember the Garden and desire it; and whenever they proceed toward evil, they remember the Fire and turn away from it. Or: the companion (al-sahib) is the owner of a thing. It is as though the Garden is their possession; they have possessed it and obtained its keys through the righteous deeds they sent forward.

The meaning of ﴿today﴾ is: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Occupied﴾ [Ya-Sin: 55], i.e., in a bliss that occupies them from anything else. Or: occupied away from their acquaintances and relatives who entered the Fire, God forbid, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all﴾ [Luqman: 33]. So they are in a bliss that occupies them from all of these, as though they do not know them.

﴿Fakihun﴾: it is said: fakih and fakih, meaning: one who enjoys pleasure and luxury. From it comes al-fakiha (fruit); it is not among the necessities, rather it comes from tafakkuh (enjoyment and delight).

As for His, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿They and their spouses are in shade, reclining upon couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56]: I recall that when I recited this verse to the brethren, one of them struck his chest, and he was a dignified elder, striking his chest violently and emotionally, and said: (Oh my ruin, that woman is going to come to me again!), because he saw in his wife what repelled him from her, so he was astonished that she would keep company with him even in the Hereafter and in the Garden. We said to him: O shaykh, you dislike certain things in your wife, but she has good deeds with God that make her fit for the Garden; her good deed with God cancels her bad deed with you.

Perhaps you are sharp-tempered, or greedy with a wandering eye; for God, exalted is He, said concerning married life: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy﴾ [al-Rum: 21].

So married life at its beginning is a dwelling (sakan), where each of the two inclines to the other and finds rest in his embrace. Then, when circumstances change and one of them loses interest in the other, or something repellent appears from him, there is affection; and if old age and infirmity afflict them both, let each show mercy to the other's weakness, by the mercy God placed between them. Married life in this state is a living of mercy above all else.

Then this wife, of whom you resent some qualities and whose conduct repels you, will not come in the Hereafter in this form that you dislike; rather she will come in a new form, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And purified spouses﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 15]. So God will purify her of what you used to hold against her.

The meaning of ﴿in shade﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56] is: there is no sun there, and no heat that harms them. Shade is known, which the responsible ones (mukallafun) are accustomed to in this world, and to it they retreat from the heat of the sun; it is a familiar matter to them. But in the Hereafter, these are shades in which they are given enjoyment, or in the shade of God, as the noble hadith reports. And al-ara'ik: plural of arika, which is a couch that has a canopy (hajalah) (al-namusiyya), or: it is the cushion upon which one reclines.

The meaning of ﴿reclining﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56]: reclining is a state and posture of a person; he is either standing, or sitting, or reclining, and reclining is the most pleasurable of these states, because the one standing is standing for work, and the one sitting sits for a worry he is thinking about, so he is neither able to rise for work nor able to recline for rest. Therefore His, glory be to Him, saying ﴿reclining﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56] means: complete rest for them.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿For them therein﴾ [Ya-Sin: 57], i.e., in the Garden, ﴿is fruit﴾ [Ya-Sin: 57]. Fruit comes from tafakkuh (enjoyment and delight). We know that a person eats food either for sustenance, which is the necessities, or as fruit for delight and luxury; and here the Real, glory be to Him, mentions only fruit, because in the Garden we eat only for enjoyment and luxury, not out of need or hunger.

﴿And for them is whatever they call for﴾ [Ya-Sin: 57], i.e., whatever they ask for and whatever occurs to their minds, they find it before them. Some have said: (whatever they call for) means that God does not withhold any request from them, because He, glory be to Him, gives them before they ask.

After that, the Real, exalted is He, speaks about a meaning He wanted for His creation in this world as a result of following His method and His straight path, so He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58]. The fruit of Islam is that they surrender their reins entirely to the hand of their Creator, that they be brothers worshipping one deity, and that they live together in security, tranquility and peace.

So, security and peace are the goal of God's method, and they are the completion of blessing; otherwise, if a person enjoyed every kind of bliss but lost the blessing of security and peace, all blessings would be embittered for him, and he would not be content with a life nor enjoy any pleasure. Therefore God, exalted is He, bestowed favour upon the Quraysh, saying: ﴿Who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear﴾ [Quraysh: 4].

Peace (salam) is from you when you turn toward another and say: "al-salamu 'alaykum," meaning: I turn to you with peace; and he replies: "wa 'alaykumu al-salam," and the meaning is: neither do you harm us, nor do we harm you. Each is given peace according to his capacity. But when peace is from God, it is absolute peace, the peace that protects you on all your sides, so that nothing harmful reaches you.

The meaning of ﴿Peace, a word﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58] is: God, exalted is He, is its speaker, not a message transmitted through angels, for example, saying to them: "Greet so-and-so." The meaning is: peace, being a word from a Lord, Most Merciful, and not a communication from God through anyone. He chose here the term lordship (rububiyya), which requires that the one who nurtures loves the one nurtured. How much more so when lordship is described with mercy: ﴿from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58].

After the Real, glory be to Him, has told us about the believers and the bliss awaiting them, He tells us about the criminals:

﴿And withdraw today, O you criminals...﴾.

Then He, glorified is He, says: "For them therein" — that is, in Paradise — "is fruit" (fākihah). Fākihah derives from tafakkuh, meaning enjoyment and delight. We know that a person eats food either for sustenance, which is the necessities, or as fruit for pleasure and luxury. Here the Almighty mentions only fruit, because in Paradise we eat only for enjoyment and luxury, not out of need or hunger.

﴿And for them is whatever they call for﴾ — that is, whatever they ask for and whatever comes to their minds, and they find it before them. Some of them said: "(Mā yaddaʻūn)" means: God does not withhold from them a supplication, because He, glorified is He, gives them before they ask.

Next, the Exalted Lord speaks about the meaning He intended for His creatures in this world, as the result of following His method and His straight path. So He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Peace! A word from a Lord Most Merciful.﴾ The fruit of Islam is that people surrender their reins entirely into the hand of their Creator, that they become brothers worshipping one single Object of worship, and that they live together in security, tranquility and peace.

So, security and peace are the goal of God's method, and they are the completion of blessing. Otherwise, if a person enjoyed every kind of pleasure but lost the blessing of security and peace, all blessings would be embittered for him, and he would find no pleasure in life nor enjoyment in any delight. Therefore God, exalted is He, bestowed His favor upon the Quraysh, saying: ﴿Who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴾ [Quraysh: 4].

Peace comes from you when you turn toward another and say: "As-salamu 'alaykum" (peace be upon you), meaning: "I come to you in peace." He replies: "Wa 'alaykumu as-salam" (and upon you be peace). The meaning is: neither do you harm us, nor do we harm you. Each one gives peace according to his capacity. But when peace comes from God, it is absolute peace, the peace that protects you from every side, so that nothing harmful reaches you.

As for the meaning of ﴿Peace, a word﴾: it means that God Himself is the One who speaks it, not a message conveyed through the angels, for example, by Him saying to them: "Convey peace to so-and-so." So the meaning is: peace, being a word from a Lord Most Merciful, and not a communication delivered from God by anyone. He chose here the term "Lordship," which requires that the one who nurtures loves the one he nurtures; so what of when you describe the Lordship with mercy: ﴿from a Lord Most Merciful﴾.

Meaning of ﴿Withdraw yourselves﴾ [Yasin: 59]: that is, separate yourselves, O criminals, from the believers, and withdraw far away from them; gather together on one side so that you may see the believers entering Paradise, while you remain in the place of standing so that your regret may increase.

The wisdom of God Most High required that the believers and the disbelievers be distinguished, meaning that each of them be recognised. This occurred at the Battle of Hudaybiyah. Before they returned to Madinah, God made clear to them the wisdom in this and the reason behind the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, and why the Messenger of God (ﷺ) accepted its conditions. The reason was that among the disbelievers of Makkah there were believers who concealed their faith, and no one knew them. Had the Muslims entered Makkah at that time, clashes would have occurred between the two sides, and these believers who concealed their faith, unable to declare it openly, would have been harmed, and the innocent would have been seized along with the guilty.

For this reason, the Exalted said in this account in Surah al-Fath: ﴿They are those who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque and the offering detained from reaching its place of sacrifice. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and there would befall you because of them a blemish without knowledge — [that God might admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment]﴾ [al-Fath: 25]. The meaning of ﴿they had been separated﴾ [al-Fath: 25] is: if the believers had been distinguished from the disbelievers.

Or the meaning may be: ﴿And withdraw yourselves today, O criminals﴾ [Yasin: 59], that is, separate yourselves by the marks of your distinction, which will be with you constantly, such that your shame before us now is not the only thing; rather, you will have features by which you are recognised. This mark is the mark of anger and blackness of face, God forbid. Of this is the Exalted's saying concerning the believers: ﴿You recognise them by their mark﴾ [al-Baqarah: 273].

As if a questioner asked: Do the disbelievers deserve all this punishment and this anger from Allah, exalted is He? The Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, answers: Yes, they deserve it, because Allah warned them and cautioned them, and they did not respond. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan?﴾

So Allah, glory be to Him, did not seize you unawares; rather, He warned you and made clear to you the entrances of Satan, his snares, and his stratagems...

After Our Lord, blessed and exalted, forbade us from worshipping Satan, He directs us to the true worship: "And that you worship Me. This is a straight path" (Qur'an 36:61). When we reflect on these two verses, we find that the reason for the prohibition against worshipping Satan is: "Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy" (Qur'an 36:60). The expected parallel in the verse that follows would be: "And that you worship Me, because I am your beloved..."

But the Truth, glorified is He, did not ground His worship in love. Rather, [He says]: "Worship Me, because I call you to the straight path, which benefits you and organizes your lives. Worship Me for this. As for the matter of love, it exists, and I love you. Whether I love you or I do not love you, it was incumbent upon you to follow this straight path, because you are the one who benefits from it."

The Mountain (al-Jibilla): they are the strong, mighty people. Whenever you encounter the root (j-b-l), know that it indicates strength, firmness, steadiness and grandeur, and from this the mountain (al-jabal) was so named for its steadfastness. We say: "So-and-so was created (jubila) upon such-and-such," meaning: it is an original trait in him, fixed in his character. Thus these things share one common derivational link, and for this reason we liken the wise man to a mountain, because he is steadfast and is not shaken by events.

The meaning of "And he had already led astray a great multitude from among you. Did you not then use your reason?" is: you are not the first whom Iblis misled. He had led astray before you many peoples who were stronger than you, and he played with them until he made them tools of misguidance. He did not stop at their own misguidance; rather, they went astray and led others astray, until they became soldiers of his army, as we have said...

Then the Real (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, rebukes these disobedient ones: "Did you not then use your reason?" meaning: where were your minds when you followed him, after We had warned you against him and explained to you his entry points? When your Creator returns you to reason and commands you to exercise it, know that the outcome of exercising reason agrees with His purpose for you, glory be to Him. If you employ your reason in the cosmos of God and His signs, you must arrive at a result intended by God, Exalted is He. Likewise, you do not instruct your interlocutor to use his reason on something unless you are confident that the outcome of this exercise is in your favour and in accordance with your desire. Had you known that the result was contrary to what you want, you would not have given him the opportunity to use his reason.

We illustrated this with the seller who offers a good commodity: he invites you to inspect it, examine it and make sure of its quality... As for the cheat, he tries to persuade you with theoretical talk, most of it lies and deception, and tries to divert your mind and thought from the matter, because the outcome will not be in his favour.

Likewise, the Real, glory be to Him, says: "Did you not then use your reason?" meaning: if you had reasoned, you would have reached the truth and the straight path.

Here too, he considers the warning of Hell to be a promise, not a threat. We have already learned that promise is used for good, and threat for evil...

And we said: it is called a promise because warning against evil before falling into it is regarded as good, since you are able to remedy the matter and correct the mistake.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 36, verses 64–65:

Here too he considers the warning of Hell to be a promise (wa'd) and not a threat (wa'id). We have already noted that wa'd is used for good and wa'id for evil, and among the examples is the words of the poet:

O Time, O you who carry out your threats,
and who fail the hopes placed in your promise.

We said: it is called a promise because warning against evil before falling into it is considered a good, since you are able to remedy the matter and correct the error.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Burn therein today﴾ [Yasin: 64], i.e., enter it, roast yourselves in its fire, and be burned by its flames. ﴿Today﴾ [Yasin: 64], i.e., the Day of Recompense, the present day in which you are. As for what came before it, it has passed, and the pleasures that brought you to the Fire have passed with it. The pleasures have gone and their consequences remain, and nothing is left before you but the Fire in which you will burn ﴿for what you used to disbelieve﴾ [Yasin: 64]. That is: this Fire is not an injustice; rather, it is the recompense for your disbelief in the blessing of God. This is a rebuke to them, because they did not recognise the blessings of the Truth, glorified is He, upon them; and had they recognised this blessing of God, they would not have disbelieved in it.

Therefore, when you do good to a person and he repays your kindness with evil, he is ashamed to face you, and he can bear any punishment from you except that you confront him yourself. Why? Because the shame of the wrongdoer before the benefactor is harder upon him than punishment. So it is as if God, exalted is He, is saying to these disbelievers in His blessings: be ashamed before God, for He has bestowed blessings upon you and you have disbelieved in them; and if you had any feeling, your being reminded of your disbelief would be harder on you than this Fire which you are burning in.

Then He, glorified is He, describes their state, may God protect us: ﴿Today We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Yasin: 65].

His saying ﴿Today﴾ [Yasin: 65], i.e., the Day of Resurrection and recompense, ﴿We shall seal their mouths﴾ [Yasin: 65].

We close them so that they cannot speak. The mouths are the seat of speech. Before God seals their mouths in the Hereafter, He sealed their hearts in this world: yesterday God sealed the hearts so that no faith enters them and no disbelief leaves them; today God has sealed the mouths and prevented them from speaking, so that they neither offer excuses nor seek forgiveness.

The station here is one of reckoning, not of action, so there is no benefit from seeking forgiveness and no use in making excuses. Rather, the time of speech and argument has ended, and the tongue has no further role. Today the mouths are shut and the tongues are restrained, so that the limbs may speak.

Now reflect upon what follows: ﴿Their hands will speak to Us and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Yasin: 65]. Analogy would have required that the Truth, glorified is He, say: "Today We shall seal their mouths," and [then] "We shall make their hands speak and We shall make their feet bear witness", but the Qur'anic context here is different. After God seals their mouths, their hands speak to Us voluntarily, not by command, and their feet bear witness voluntarily, not by command. We did not say to the hands, "Speak," nor did We say to the feet, "Bear witness."

Rather, these limbs volunteered to bear witness, even though they are the very limbs through which sins and wrongdoings were committed in the world. Yet they bear witness not against themselves, but against the conscious self, which God had subjected the limbs to, and commanded them to proceed according to its will, and to be at its beck and call in the world.

As for now, in the Hereafter, the limbs have been freed from their subordination to the conscious self, and all sovereignty and authority belong entirely to God, exalted is He. So now the limbs speak what they wish, and bear witness to what was before the Lord Most High, glorified is He.

We have previously illustrated this matter with the battalion of an army which the supreme commander sends out; the battalion must obey the orders of its immediate commander, even if the orders are mistaken, until it returns to the higher authority and complains to him of what the immediate commander did. So it is with the limbs on the Day of Resurrection.

If you say: why was speech attributed to the hands and testimony to the feet? We say: because the bulk of actions is customarily attributed to the hands, even if walking was the means of the act; and since the hands speak, they become like a claimant who needs a witness, so the feet bear witness.

As for the question of how the hands will speak: He who made the tongue, which is a piece of flesh and blood, speak, is able to make the other limbs speak, the hands or others. And since the act belongs to God, there is no need to ask about the manner. Moreover, the hands contain more nerves than the organs of speech.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ [Yasin: 65], and He did not say "for what they used to do," this is because there is a difference between a person who engages in sin but does not rejoice in it, rather regrets it and punishes himself for committing it, and another who regards committing sin as a gain, rejoices in it, speaks of it and boasts of committing it.

As for the linguistic investigation of the root (k-s-b): this verb comes in its unaugmented form (kasaba), and it denotes profit in buying and selling, and it denotes work that proceeds from a person naturally, without strain or artifice, and it is most often used for good.

This verb also comes in its augmented form with the hamza and the taa' (iktasaba), and it denotes artifice and strain, and this form is used for sin. We clarified this point, saying: when a person does good, the act proceeds from him naturally and spontaneously; but evil he sneaks towards and schemes for, because good is easy, gentle, smooth and acceptable, whereas sin is burdensome and shameful.

When you sit, for example, among your family and see your wife, your daughters, your paternal aunt, your maternal aunt, and so on, among whom are beautiful and handsome ones, and you look at all of them without strain and without shame, because it is a natural matter. But with non-mahrams, and with those whom it is forbidden for you to look upon, you steal a glance and scheme for it, so that your situation is not exposed and no one perceives your fault.

So when kasaba comes in place of iktasaba, know that the one who commits sin and the wrongdoer has become accustomed to it and familiar with it, to the extent that he does it as if it were a natural matter, so he does not conceal it nor feel shame about it, but rather flaunts it. Thus the verb kasaba is used for him as a form of earning, as in this verse:

﴿and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Yasin: 65].

His saying ﴿Today﴾ [Yasin: 65], i.e., the Day of Resurrection and recompense, ﴿We shall seal their mouths﴾ [Yasin: 65].

We close them so that they cannot speak. The mouths are the seat of speech. Before God seals their mouths in the Hereafter, He sealed their hearts in this world: yesterday God sealed the hearts so that no faith enters them and no disbelief leaves them; today God has sealed the mouths and prevented them from speaking, so that they neither offer excuses nor seek forgiveness.

The station here is one of reckoning, not of action, so there is no benefit from seeking forgiveness and no use in making excuses. Rather, the time of speech and argument has ended, and the tongue has no further role. Today the mouths are shut and the tongues are restrained, so that the limbs may speak.

Now reflect upon what follows: ﴿Their hands will speak to Us and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Yasin: 65]. Analogy would have required that the Truth, glorified is He, say: "Today We shall seal their mouths," and [then] "We shall make their hands speak and We shall make their feet bear witness", but the Qur'anic context here is different. After God seals their mouths, their hands speak to Us voluntarily, not by command, and their feet bear witness voluntarily, not by command. We did not say to the hands, "Speak," nor did We say to the feet, "Bear witness."

Rather, these limbs volunteered to bear witness, even though they are the very limbs through which sins and wrongdoings were committed in the world. Yet they bear witness not against themselves, but against the conscious self, which God had subjected the limbs to, and commanded them to proceed according to its will, and to be at its beck and call in the world.

As for now, in the Hereafter, the limbs have been freed from their subordination to the conscious self, and all sovereignty and authority belong entirely to God, exalted is He. So now the limbs speak what they wish, and bear witness to what was before the Lord Most High, glorified is He.

We have previously illustrated this matter with the battalion of an army which the supreme commander sends out; the battalion must obey the orders of its immediate commander, even if the orders are mistaken, until it returns to the higher authority and complains to him of what the immediate commander did. So it is with the limbs on the Day of Resurrection.

If you say: why was speech attributed to the hands and testimony to the feet? We say: because the bulk of actions is customarily attributed to the hands, even if walking was the means of the act; and since the hands speak, they become like a claimant who needs a witness, so the feet bear witness.

As for the question of how the hands will speak: He who made the tongue, which is a piece of flesh and blood, speak, is able to make the other limbs speak, the hands or others. And since the act belongs to God, there is no need to ask about the manner. Moreover, the hands contain more nerves than the organs of speech.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ [Yasin: 65], and He did not say "for what they used to do," this is because there is a difference between a person who engages in sin but does not rejoice in it, rather regrets it and punishes himself for committing it, and another who regards committing sin as a gain, rejoices in it, speaks of it and boasts of committing it.

As for the linguistic investigation of the root (k-s-b): this verb comes in its unaugmented form (kasaba), and it denotes profit in buying and selling, and it denotes work that proceeds from a person naturally, without strain or artifice, and it is most often used for good.

This verb also comes in its augmented form with the hamza and the taa' (iktasaba), and it denotes artifice and strain, and this form is used for sin. We clarified this point, saying: when a person does good, the act proceeds from him naturally and spontaneously; but evil he sneaks towards and schemes for, because good is easy, gentle, smooth and acceptable, whereas sin is burdensome and shameful.

When you sit, for example, among your family and see your wife, your daughters, your paternal aunt, your maternal aunt, and so on, among whom are beautiful and handsome ones, and you look at all of them without strain and without shame, because it is a natural matter. But with non-mahrams, and with those whom it is forbidden for you to look upon, you steal a glance and scheme for it, so that your situation is not exposed and no one perceives your fault.

So when kasaba comes in place of iktasaba, know that the one who commits sin and the wrongdoer has become accustomed to it and familiar with it, to the extent that he does it as if it were a natural matter, so he does not conceal it nor feel shame about it, but rather flaunts it. Thus the verb kasaba is used for him as a form of earning, as in this verse:

﴿and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Yasin: 65].

Meaning: just as We sealed their mouths and prevented them from speaking, if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, that is, closed them and smoothed them over, such that no trace of them would appear on their faces. And if We obliterated their eyes, they would lose sight. So how would they see, when they are racing toward the path (al-sirat)?

One might say: if they lose their sight on the path, they may still have substitutes and stratagems that help them, such as feeling their way with a staff, for example, or finding someone to take their hand and guide them. So the Truth, glory be to Him, encircles them from all their sides and cuts off their hope of salvation, and says: ﴿And had We willed, We would have transformed them in their places﴾ [Ya-Sin: 67].

So the matter does not end at blindness and the obliteration of the eyes; rather there is something worse: that He would disfigure them in their places and freeze them there, so that they cannot move.

Al-maskh (transformation) means that they become like statues (al-masakhit) that do not move; or, "We transformed them" means: We changed their forms into ugly forms, as humiliation and degradation for them.

The first meaning is more apt, because He, exalted is He, said after it: ﴿So they were not able to proceed, nor could they return﴾ [Ya-Sin: 67].

Because they have frozen in their places, they have no movement, neither forward by proceeding on the new path they are facing, nor even returning on the path by which they came and to which they were accustomed.

So there is no excuse for them when they disbelieve in Allah and obey and worship Satan. Yet they may offer an excuse from another angle, saying, "O Lord, You took us, and had we lived we would have been guided and returned to the Straight Path." He is then exactly like a child, needing someone to carry him, feed him and remove harm from him, and so on. So in this state, is there any return? Does reflection and contemplation benefit him in this condition?

The matter of Oneness is a practical, rational matter, because God, exalted is He, declared that He is the true God, that He is One with no partner, that He alone is the Creator, that He is the Provider, and that He alone deserves to be worshipped. This is a claim that has faced no opposition, and a claim stands for its maker until another claims it, and we have not seen anyone claim creation for himself.

So if there were with Him, glorified is He, another god or other gods, where are they? Why did they not demand their right in this matter? Or did they remain silent about it, or were they unaware of it? In any of these states they are not fit to be gods.
