Thus: Tawhid is the original foundation of religion, but I do not know by reason what God requires of me. A messenger must be sent to me to address me with what my Lord requires of me. Therefore, a messenger is necessary. This is the second objective of religion. The address of the Truth to creation is an absolute perfection, and humans are an absolute deficiency; therefore this address necessarily requires an intermediary able to receive from that absolute perfection and able to convey to those of lesser perfection. Thus the matter proceeds in gradation: Allah addresses the angels, the angels address the messengers, and the messengers address the people.

So there must be (risalah, messengership), which is the second objective of religion, and the Messenger is the intermediary between the Creator and the created. The Messenger is not merely a conveyer, but a conveyer, a model of conduct and practice, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21]. Had the Messenger been an angel, the exemplary model would not have been realized in him, and I could not be held to what the Messenger requires unless the Messenger were of my own kind.

Therefore, the Most High, explaining this issue, says: ﴿And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said: Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾ [al-Isra: 94]. The response comes: "Say" (qul), i.e., as a reply to them: ﴿If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 95].

Thus: how would we send down an angel to humans? If the angel descended in his luminous nature, humans would not see him, and he must come to them in human form. Otherwise the doubt would remain: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them about what they confuse﴾ [al-An'am: 9].

Therefore, there must be - then - intermediaries that are most like the (transformer) in the world of electricity, which is a device that takes from powerful forces and gives to the weak without burning it.

The third element of religion is the Resurrection (hashr), because the message came to carry the method: do this and do not do that. Among people, some will follow this method, doing what is commanded and refraining from what is forbidden, and some will turn away from it and even oppose it. Thus there must be a return in which the obedient is rewarded and the opponent is punished. This return is the Resurrection.

The Truth, glorified is He, spoke of Tawhid in His saying: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60-61], and He spoke of the Resurrection in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised. Burn in it today for what you used to disbelieve﴾ [Ya-Sin: 63-64].

Now He speaks of the second element, which is the messengership (risalah), so we say about His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]. That is: We, not the society or the environment in which he lived. Therefore, illiteracy in the Messenger of Allah was an honour, because if he had not been illiterate, his culture would have come from creation.

As for his illiteracy, it means he took his culture and knowledge from Allah. Therefore it was of his honour, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he be illiterate, and of the honour of his nation that it be illiterate, because if it had been a learned nation, it would have been said that what happened in the Arabian Peninsula was merely a civilizational leap, just as they said: "When Allah gave us victory in the Ramadan War, and we saw with our own eyes Allah's support for us, yet they said: a civilizational victory."

So the Truth, glorified is He, establishes this reality: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]; had We taught him, it would have been something other than poetry. The Messenger of Allah is indeed taught, but taught by whom? By his Lord. He took nothing from humans.

It may be thought that Allah did not teach him poetry because poetry requires linguistic culture and knowledge of metres and rhymes, and needs a refined sense and a musical ear, along with the other tools a poet needs, and perhaps these tools were not available to the Messenger of Allah, just as they were not available to many others besides him.

So Allah, exalted is He, rejects this assumption and says: ﴿nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69], meaning: We did not teach him poetry because of a deficiency in his abilities. Had he wished to say poetry, he would have said it in the finest way it can be said; but it is not befitting for him to do so, because the mission of the Messenger differs from the mission of the poet. Most poetry is in falsehood and evil, and when it enters good it becomes weak and soft. That is because the nature of poetry is to soar and fly in imagination, and for the poet to say whatever pleases him, whatever his aim; therefore they said: the sweetest poetry is the most false.

We often see poets who are men of principle, and the foolish person finds it hard to combine the demands of faith from them with what the faculty of poetry calls them to. So they can only confine themselves to poetry of values, ethics and virtues, and keep away from satire and love poetry.

The poet of the Mahjar (diaspora), known for piety and righteousness, tried to combine this piety with his poetic talent, and said:

My Master, I disobeyed You deliberately,
so that I might see You most beautiful when forgiving.

And I gathered from sins their greatest,
out of sparing Your pardon from being small.

He excelled in the first and did not succeed in the second.

As for our master Hassan ibn Thabit, he was an excellent poet in the pre-Islamic era. When he embraced Islam, they said to him: "Your poetry has softened, O Abu al-Husam." He said: "Poetry is ill-omened; it grows strong in evil, and when it enters good it becomes weak and soft."

So His saying, the Most High: ﴿nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69] repels from the Messenger of Allah the accusation that his nature is not poetic, or that he is not sensitive of feeling, or that his ear is not musical, and all that nonsense. How could he be accused of this, when Allah taught him and revelation came into his ears?

As for the claim that the Messenger of Allah recited poetry: yes, the Messenger of Allah did recite poetry, but he did not recite it correctly; rather, he deviated in it so that the line would not remain in its correct metre. When he recited:

"The days will reveal to you what you did not know,
and there will come to you one whom you did not provide with news."

It was also reported that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "The truest word ever spoken by Labid is:

Surely everything except Allah is vain,
and every bliss is certainly bound to pass away."

The correct form is:

Surely everything except Allah is vain,
and every bliss is bound to pass away, without doubt."

So our master, the Messenger of Allah, would break the metre of the line, lest it be said that he recited poetry; although Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]; yet the Messenger of Allah was not forbidden from reciting it. It is as if the Messenger of Allah was being cautious about the matter, so he would say it, and not recite it, to keep far from it altogether.

That concerns reciting; as for his composing poetry himself, some hold that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did compose verse, such as his saying at the Battle of Hunayn:

"I am the Prophet, no lie;
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

Yes, this saying came from the Messenger of Allah agreeing with a poetic metre called rajaz. It was a statement that happened to match a poetic metre, and there is a difference between composing speech and subjecting it to metre and rhyme, and speech that happens to match a metre without intention. Otherwise there are verses in the Qur'an itself that happened to match a poetic metre; shall we say they are poetry? Read, for example: ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend of what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran: 92]. ﴿That is the one about whom you blamed me﴾ [Yusuf: 32]. ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Hijr: 49].

These and others are verses that happened to match a poetic metre, but they are not called poetry, because poetry is measured, rhymed speech intentionally composed.

The Truth, glorified is He, related that the disbelievers accused His Messenger, saying: "A sorcerer" and "a poet," and they said: "a soothsayer." But the Qur'an answered them regarding poetry and negated that the Messenger says poetry: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]. It did not negate sorcery or soothsaying from him. Why?

They said: because the mission of the Messenger of Allah is to convey the Qur'an from Allah, and the Qur'an is of the kind of elevated styles, and the closest thing to it is poetry, so the Qur'an negated it. As for sorcery, it is enigmas and speech with no meaning; therefore it did not say: "And We did not teach him sorcery."

Had this word had a referent, the reply to it would be easy: if Muhammad were a sorcerer who bewitched those who believe in him, why did he not bewitch you as well? So your denial of him and your disbelief in him is the strongest proof that he is not a sorcerer. And does the bewitched have any will with the sorcerer?

In their saying "soothsayer" there is a rebuttal to them: ﴿nor the word of a soothsayer﴾ [al-Haqqah: 42], because the soothsayer's speech is rhymed prose (saj') of a cold kind, while the Qur'an is different from all this. Moreover, you are a people of eloquence and clarity, and you are the most knowledgeable of people about styles and distinguishing between them. Would it be hidden from you to distinguish between the Qur'an and other speech, when you are a nation of speech, and you make markets and fairs for words?

Then the Truth, glorified is He, explains the reason the Messenger does not compose poetry, saying: ﴿It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]. Here "in" (in) means the negative "ma". That is: this Qur'an is nothing but a reminder to whoever has understanding, and a clear Qur'an, that is: manifest and evident, which is recited, and it may have a melody sweeter to the ear of the pious than poetry. Therefore some people hear the Qur'an and are seized by ecstasy and admiration, and if you asked them, you would find they do not know what is happening to them. Why?

They said: because the One who speaks is Allah, and the one who hears is a creature of Allah. Allah, exalted is He, speaks with speech that affects and attracts the creature who is still upon the fitrah on which people were created. If he departs from this fitrah, the Qur'an does not affect him in this way, because the Qur'an is one, but the receiving nature varies.

The Truth, glorified is He, explains this matter to us in His saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those given knowledge: "What did he just say?"﴾ [Muhammad: 16]. So Allah commanded him to reply to them: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing; and for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

That is because the doer of a thing is not its receiver. We have previously illustrated this with a cup of hot tea: you blow on it to cool it, and in winter you blow into your hands to warm them. The breath is one, but the recipients differ. So it is with people in receiving the Qur'an: whoever receives the speech of Allah with a sound fitrah understands it and is affected by it, and whoever receives the speech of Allah while preoccupied with other things is closed off, so he does not understand from Allah and is not affected by His speech.

Therefore we see some non-Arab people who do not utter a single Arabic word, yet when they hear or read the speech of Allah you see them overcome with emotion, and their eyes weep. Why? Something in their make-up must have been affected by this style.

If the Truth, glorified is He, has revealed to inanimate matter and it was moved by His speech, and revealed to animals and they understood Him, then by greater right He speaks to the rational human with speech that meets his nature and affects him, so that he is affected and moved.

Then He, glorified is He, says, explaining the mission of this Reminder and this clear Qur'an: ﴿That it may warn whoever is alive﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70]. Yes, He called them "alive," and your addressing them is proof that they are alive; but these are the living of material life, which ends in death. There is another life, of the intellect, thought, and spiritual values, and the effect of this does not appear until after death.

All people share in material life; therefore the element that enters material life to give it the character of spiritual life is called (the spirit, al-ruh). The spirit is a spirit from His command, glorified is He. After He gives the spirit by which matter lives, He gives the spirit by which values live. We have said that the life of values raises you up to give you worth in the Hereafter, and it may give you in this world peace of mind, uprightness and stability; but the true life remains in the Hereafter.

If Allah wills, a person may be given a connected life, as was given to our master Yahya. When our master Zakariyya called upon his Lord: ﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with grey, and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord. And indeed I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren; so grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub; and make him, my Lord, pleasing"﴾ [Maryam: 4-6].

Allah answered him: ﴿O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not given this name to anyone before﴾ [Maryam: 7].

So Allah gave him good tidings of a boy, and named him with a name that indicates he would give him a connected life. When you name your son "intelligent," for example, hoping he will be intelligent, or "noble," hoping he will be noble, can you make that wish come true?

Therefore the poet said:

I named him Yahya, so that he might live, but there was no way
to turn back the decree of Allah concerning him.

Yes, you named him, but you do not grant life; the Giver of life is Allah. So when Allah names someone Yahya, he must live a connected life. That is why our master Yahya died a martyr, so that his worldly life would be joined to the life of the Hereafter, and so that what Allah willed for him would be fulfilled in him.

The meaning of: ﴿and the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70] is that the punishment becomes due to them, because they did not benefit from the warning.

Then after this, the Truth, glorified is He, speaks about some of His signs in the universe:

﴿Do they not see that We created for them, from what Our hands have done, ...﴾.

The response comes: "Say" (qul), i.e., as a reply to them: ﴿If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 95].

Thus: how would we send down an angel to humans? If the angel descended in his luminous nature, humans would not see him, and he must come to them in human form. Otherwise the doubt would remain: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them about what they confuse﴾ [al-An'am: 9].

Therefore, there must be - then - intermediaries that are most like the (transformer) in the world of electricity, which is a device that takes from powerful forces and gives to the weak without burning it.

The third element of religion is the Resurrection (hashr), because the message came to carry the method: do this and do not do that. Among people, some will follow this method, doing what is commanded and refraining from what is forbidden, and some will turn away from it and even oppose it. Thus there must be a return in which the obedient is rewarded and the opponent is punished. This return is the Resurrection.

The Truth, glorified is He, spoke of Tawhid in His saying: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60-61], and He spoke of the Resurrection in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised. Burn in it today for what you used to disbelieve﴾ [Ya-Sin: 63-64].

Now He speaks of the second element, which is the messengership (risalah), so we say about His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]. That is: We, not the society or the environment in which he lived. Therefore, illiteracy in the Messenger of Allah was an honour, because if he had not been illiterate, his culture would have come from creation.

As for his illiteracy, it means he took his culture and knowledge from Allah. Therefore it was of his honour, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he be illiterate, and of the honour of his nation that it be illiterate, because if it had been a learned nation, it would have been said that what happened in the Arabian Peninsula was merely a civilizational leap, just as they said: "When Allah gave us victory in the Ramadan War, and we saw with our own eyes Allah's support for us, yet they said: a civilizational victory."

So the Truth, glorified is He, establishes this reality: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]; had We taught him, it would have been something other than poetry. The Messenger of Allah is indeed taught, but taught by whom? By his Lord. He took nothing from humans.

It may be thought that Allah did not teach him poetry because poetry requires linguistic culture and knowledge of metres and rhymes, and needs a refined sense and a musical ear, along with the other tools a poet needs, and perhaps these tools were not available to the Messenger of Allah, just as they were not available to many others besides him.

So Allah, exalted is He, rejects this assumption and says: ﴿nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69], meaning: We did not teach him poetry because of a deficiency in his abilities. Had he wished to say poetry, he would have said it in the finest way it can be said; but it is not befitting for him to do so, because the mission of the Messenger differs from the mission of the poet. Most poetry is in falsehood and evil, and when it enters good it becomes weak and soft. That is because the nature of poetry is to soar and fly in imagination, and for the poet to say whatever pleases him, whatever his aim; therefore they said: the sweetest poetry is the most false.

We often see poets who are men of principle, and the foolish person finds it hard to combine the demands of faith from them with what the faculty of poetry calls them to. So they can only confine themselves to poetry of values, ethics and virtues, and keep away from satire and love poetry.

The poet of the Mahjar (diaspora), known for piety and righteousness, tried to combine this piety with his poetic talent, and said:

My Master, I disobeyed You deliberately,
so that I might see You most beautiful when forgiving.

And I gathered from sins their greatest,
out of sparing Your pardon from being small.

He excelled in the first and did not succeed in the second.

As for our master Hassan ibn Thabit, he was an excellent poet in the pre-Islamic era. When he embraced Islam, they said to him: "Your poetry has softened, O Abu al-Husam." He said: "Poetry is ill-omened; it grows strong in evil, and when it enters good it becomes weak and soft."

So His saying, the Most High: ﴿nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69] repels from the Messenger of Allah the accusation that his nature is not poetic, or that he is not sensitive of feeling, or that his ear is not musical, and all that nonsense. How could he be accused of this, when Allah taught him and revelation came into his ears?

As for the claim that the Messenger of Allah recited poetry: yes, the Messenger of Allah did recite poetry, but he did not recite it correctly; rather, he deviated in it so that the line would not remain in its correct metre. When he recited:

"The days will reveal to you what you did not know,
and there will come to you one whom you did not provide with news."

It was also reported that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "The truest word ever spoken by Labid is:

Surely everything except Allah is vain,
and every bliss is certainly bound to pass away."

The correct form is:

Surely everything except Allah is vain,
and every bliss is bound to pass away, without doubt."

So our master, the Messenger of Allah, would break the metre of the line, lest it be said that he recited poetry; although Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]; yet the Messenger of Allah was not forbidden from reciting it. It is as if the Messenger of Allah was being cautious about the matter, so he would say it, and not recite it, to keep far from it altogether.

That concerns reciting; as for his composing poetry himself, some hold that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did compose verse, such as his saying at the Battle of Hunayn:

"I am the Prophet, no lie;
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

Yes, this saying came from the Messenger of Allah agreeing with a poetic metre called rajaz. It was a statement that happened to match a poetic metre, and there is a difference between composing speech and subjecting it to metre and rhyme, and speech that happens to match a metre without intention. Otherwise there are verses in the Qur'an itself that happened to match a poetic metre; shall we say they are poetry? Read, for example: ﴿You will not attain righteousness until you spend of what you love﴾ [Al 'Imran: 92]. ﴿That is the one about whom you blamed me﴾ [Yusuf: 32]. ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Hijr: 49].

These and others are verses that happened to match a poetic metre, but they are not called poetry, because poetry is measured, rhymed speech intentionally composed.

The Truth, glorified is He, related that the disbelievers accused His Messenger, saying: "A sorcerer" and "a poet," and they said: "a soothsayer." But the Qur'an answered them regarding poetry and negated that the Messenger says poetry: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]. It did not negate sorcery or soothsaying from him. Why?

They said: because the mission of the Messenger of Allah is to convey the Qur'an from Allah, and the Qur'an is of the kind of elevated styles, and the closest thing to it is poetry, so the Qur'an negated it. As for sorcery, it is enigmas and speech with no meaning; therefore it did not say: "And We did not teach him sorcery."

Had this word had a referent, the reply to it would be easy: if Muhammad were a sorcerer who bewitched those who believe in him, why did he not bewitch you as well? So your denial of him and your disbelief in him is the strongest proof that he is not a sorcerer. And does the bewitched have any will with the sorcerer?

In their saying "soothsayer" there is a rebuttal to them: ﴿nor the word of a soothsayer﴾ [al-Haqqah: 42], because the soothsayer's speech is rhymed prose (saj') of a cold kind, while the Qur'an is different from all this. Moreover, you are a people of eloquence and clarity, and you are the most knowledgeable of people about styles and distinguishing between them. Would it be hidden from you to distinguish between the Qur'an and other speech, when you are a nation of speech, and you make markets and fairs for words?

Then the Truth, glorified is He, explains the reason the Messenger does not compose poetry, saying: ﴿It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]. Here "in" (in) means the negative "ma". That is: this Qur'an is nothing but a reminder to whoever has understanding, and a clear Qur'an, that is: manifest and evident, which is recited, and it may have a melody sweeter to the ear of the pious than poetry. Therefore some people hear the Qur'an and are seized by ecstasy and admiration, and if you asked them, you would find they do not know what is happening to them. Why?

They said: because the One who speaks is Allah, and the one who hears is a creature of Allah. Allah, exalted is He, speaks with speech that affects and attracts the creature who is still upon the fitrah on which people were created. If he departs from this fitrah, the Qur'an does not affect him in this way, because the Qur'an is one, but the receiving nature varies.

The Truth, glorified is He, explains this matter to us in His saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those given knowledge: "What did he just say?"﴾ [Muhammad: 16]. So Allah commanded him to reply to them: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing; and for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

That is because the doer of a thing is not its receiver. We have previously illustrated this with a cup of hot tea: you blow on it to cool it, and in winter you blow into your hands to warm them. The breath is one, but the recipients differ. So it is with people in receiving the Qur'an: whoever receives the speech of Allah with a sound fitrah understands it and is affected by it, and whoever receives the speech of Allah while preoccupied with other things is closed off, so he does not understand from Allah and is not affected by His speech.

Therefore we see some non-Arab people who do not utter a single Arabic word, yet when they hear or read the speech of Allah you see them overcome with emotion, and their eyes weep. Why? Something in their make-up must have been affected by this style.

If the Truth, glorified is He, has revealed to inanimate matter and it was moved by His speech, and revealed to animals and they understood Him, then by greater right He speaks to the rational human with speech that meets his nature and affects him, so that he is affected and moved.

Then He, glorified is He, says, explaining the mission of this Reminder and this clear Qur'an: ﴿That it may warn whoever is alive﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70]. Yes, He called them "alive," and your addressing them is proof that they are alive; but these are the living of material life, which ends in death. There is another life, of the intellect, thought, and spiritual values, and the effect of this does not appear until after death.

All people share in material life; therefore the element that enters material life to give it the character of spiritual life is called (the spirit, al-ruh). The spirit is a spirit from His command, glorified is He. After He gives the spirit by which matter lives, He gives the spirit by which values live. We have said that the life of values raises you up to give you worth in the Hereafter, and it may give you in this world peace of mind, uprightness and stability; but the true life remains in the Hereafter.

If Allah wills, a person may be given a connected life, as was given to our master Yahya. When our master Zakariyya called upon his Lord: ﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with grey, and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord. And indeed I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren; so grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub; and make him, my Lord, pleasing"﴾ [Maryam: 4-6].

Allah answered him: ﴿O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not given this name to anyone before﴾ [Maryam: 7].

So Allah gave him good tidings of a boy, and named him with a name that indicates he would give him a connected life. When you name your son "intelligent," for example, hoping he will be intelligent, or "noble," hoping he will be noble, can you make that wish come true?

Therefore the poet said:

I named him Yahya, so that he might live, but there was no way
to turn back the decree of Allah concerning him.

Yes, you named him, but you do not grant life; the Giver of life is Allah. So when Allah names someone Yahya, he must live a connected life. That is why our master Yahya died a martyr, so that his worldly life would be joined to the life of the Hereafter, and so that what Allah willed for him would be fulfilled in him.

The meaning of: ﴿and the word may be justified against the disbelievers﴾ [Ya-Sin: 70] is that the punishment becomes due to them, because they did not benefit from the warning.

Then after this, the Truth, glorified is He, speaks about some of His signs in the universe:

﴿Do they not see that We created for them, from what Our hands have done, ...﴾.

Here the Almighty transports them into the realm of material things, which they cannot deny. We have said that the seeing in ﴿Have they not seen﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71] may be a seeing with the eye or a seeing of knowledge. ﴿That We have created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71]. The phrase ﴿of what Our hands have made﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71] negates partnership, meaning: this is Our making and Our creation, in which no one shared with Us, and no one assisted Us; rather it is a creation of Allah alone.

The word ﴿cattle﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71] (al-an'am) refers to the an'am mentioned in Surat al-An'am: ﴿Eight mates: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful. And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah instructed you with this? Then who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah to mislead the people without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-An'am: 143-144].

They are the cattle, the camels, the sheep and the goats. They are called an'am because they are the outstanding blessing in many things from which we benefit in our lives: we take from them wool, fleece, hides and milk, we load heavy burdens upon them, and all of these are clear blessings in the Arab environment.

Furthermore, the creation of the cattle is itself a blessing, and His saying ﴿so they are their owners﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71] is another blessing; for there are other wild animals that cannot be owned except by hunting and by force, and they are of little benefit compared with the domesticated ones from which man benefits, driving them, riding them and milking them.

Then there is the blessing of their subjugation: ﴿And We have subjected them to them﴾ [Ya-Sin: 72]. Otherwise, if Allah had created them without subjugating them, man would not have been able to tame them or benefit from them. The camel, for example, despite its great size and strength, is driven, made to kneel and ridden by a child; how? Because Allah subjected it and made it obedient. As for the snake, despite its small size, we fear it and flee from it, because Allah has not subjected it to us. Rather, the flea in the bed annoys you and troubles you, and you have no authority over it.

So: the creation of these cattle is itself a blessing, their being owned is a blessing, and their subjugation is a blessing, and these blessings are shared by the believer and the disbeliever alike, because they are from the gift of Lordship. Therefore, it was incumbent upon them to honour this, and to ask themselves: how do we disbelieve in Allah while He continuously bestows upon us all these blessings? And would that their disbelief stopped with themselves; rather it extends further when they prevent the messengers from spreading their call.

As for His saying: ﴿Of them is their means of riding﴾ [Ya-Sin: 72], meaning: that which is ridden of the beasts. Rakub (riding) is like our saying "a sheep that is halub", meaning: one that is milked. ﴿And of them they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 72], meaning: from their milk while they are alive, and from the milk we obtain cheese and butter, etc. ﴿And for them in them are benefits and drinks﴾ [Ya-Sin: 73]. Mashārib is the plural of mashrab. The intended meaning is the water-skin from which they used to drink, which is made from the hides of these animals; or what is intended by mashārib is what is drunk from their milk. Although milk is drunk from the female, the male is a cause of it, for had she not conceived, there would be no milk from her.

Then these blessings are concluded with His saying: ﴿Will they not then be thankful?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 73], in this interrogative style so that they themselves may answer. Allah does not say to them: "Thank Me for these blessings", rather He establishes them: Does this deserve gratitude or not? Then, if you give thanks, you will receive further gift and increase: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

So: it was obligatory upon them to thank Allah for His blessings, and these blessings should have called them to belief in this beneficent God who continuously bestows upon them outward and inward blessings. And why not? A person who is an employee receiving his wages every month from his employer must greet him every day and show him affection; so is not the One who bestows all these blessings more deserving to be worshipped and thanked?

And would that their matter ended merely at not giving thanks; rather the Qur'an relates about them, saying:

﴿And they have taken, besides Allah...﴾.

For in the horizons around man there are signs, and within himself there are signs. So whoever turns away from the first, or is heedless of them, how could he be heedless of the second, which lies within his own self and essence that never leaves him?

Therefore He, glorified be He, said: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

Yet despite this, ﴿they have taken gods besides Allah﴾ [Ya-Sin: 74], meaning: they worshipped them besides Allah. Why? ﴿That perhaps they might be helped﴾ [Ya-Sin: 74]. It is true that a person takes a god for himself to help him in his hardship. But if this god to which you turn in hardship is one who returns to you and needs you, so that you must repair it if the wind breaks it, or if accidents knock it over; if it falls, you raise it; if its arm is broken, you mend it; and if the flood comes, it sweeps it away and throws it into the mud. Then how can this be taken as a god?

You know the story of our master Ibrahim, when he smashed the idols, and he asked his people: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Ibrahim? He said: Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it; so ask them, if they can speak﴾ [al-Anbiya: 62–63].

Thus the Prophet of Allah Ibrahim (peace be upon him) confronted them with the word of truth that they could not deny: that they are deaf, lifeless objects that cannot speak. ﴿So they returned to themselves and said: Indeed you are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 64]. But soon they became alert to the danger of this admission, and returned to their former arrogance and obstinacy: ﴿Then they were turned upside down on their heads: You know well that these do not speak﴾ [al-Anbiya: 65]. At that point Ibrahim saw fit to confront them with this truth from which they were trying to escape: ﴿He said: Do you then worship besides Allah that which can neither benefit you nor harm you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 66–67].

Therefore Allah responds to them: ﴿They cannot help them, and they are a host brought forth [for them]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 75]. They cannot help their worshippers; rather, it is the worshippers who help them. On the Day of Resurrection Allah will gather them together, for the worshipper is not gathered without the worshipped, so that the confrontation may take place. Were the worshipper gathered alone, he would wait for his god to help him and defend him. Rather, all are gathered together, as He, glorified be He, said: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another? Nay, today they are submissive﴾ [as-Saffat: 25–26].

And He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship﴾ [as-Saffat: 22], meaning: bring them forward with you into the Fire, the worshipper and the worshipped. The meaning is that these idols will be fuel for the Fire by which the worshippers will be punished.

After that, the context returns to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom they arrogantly oppose and defy:

﴿So let not their saying grieve you. Indeed, We know...﴾.

Strange that the Qur'an should relate this about them after Allah had explained to them His signs that establish His supreme existence and His great oneness. For in the horizons around man there are signs, and within himself there are signs. So whoever turns away from the first, or is heedless of them, how could he be heedless of the second, which lies within his own self and essence that never leaves him?

Therefore He, glorified be He, said: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

Yet despite this, ﴿they have taken gods besides Allah﴾ [Ya-Sin: 74], meaning: they worshipped them besides Allah. Why? ﴿That perhaps they might be helped﴾ [Ya-Sin: 74]. It is true that a person takes a god for himself to help him in his hardship. But if this god to which you turn in hardship is one who returns to you and needs you, so that you must repair it if the wind breaks it, or if accidents knock it over; if it falls, you raise it; if its arm is broken, you mend it; and if the flood comes, it sweeps it away and throws it into the mud. Then how can this be taken as a god?

You know the story of our master Ibrahim, when he smashed the idols, and he asked his people: ﴿Did you do this to our gods, O Ibrahim? He said: Rather, this one, the biggest of them, did it; so ask them, if they can speak﴾ [al-Anbiya: 62–63].

Thus the Prophet of Allah Ibrahim (peace be upon him) confronted them with the word of truth that they could not deny: that they are deaf, lifeless objects that cannot speak. ﴿So they returned to themselves and said: Indeed you are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 64]. But soon they became alert to the danger of this admission, and returned to their former arrogance and obstinacy: ﴿Then they were turned upside down on their heads: You know well that these do not speak﴾ [al-Anbiya: 65]. At that point Ibrahim saw fit to confront them with this truth from which they were trying to escape: ﴿He said: Do you then worship besides Allah that which can neither benefit you nor harm you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 66–67].

Therefore Allah responds to them: ﴿They cannot help them, and they are a host brought forth [for them]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 75]. They cannot help their worshippers; rather, it is the worshippers who help them. On the Day of Resurrection Allah will gather them together, for the worshipper is not gathered without the worshipped, so that the confrontation may take place. Were the worshipper gathered alone, he would wait for his god to help him and defend him. Rather, all are gathered together, as He, glorified be He, said: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another? Nay, today they are submissive﴾ [as-Saffat: 25–26].

And He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship﴾ [as-Saffat: 22], meaning: bring them forward with you into the Fire, the worshipper and the worshipped. The meaning is that these idols will be fuel for the Fire by which the worshippers will be punished.

After that, the context returns to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom they arrogantly oppose and defy:

﴿So let not their saying grieve you. Indeed, We know...﴾.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 36, verse 76:

God Most High consoles His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and comforts his heart. Consolation can only come from one who consoles someone who is consoled. The one who consoles is the one who sent the one consoled, so He must keep him company even in hardship. God's way with all the Messengers is that God never sent a Messenger and then abandoned him. Hardship in the journey and procession of the messages has been nothing but a purification of the souls of the believers, a testing of them, and a correction of belief, so that none remains except the true believer who bears the responsibility of the message and defends it.

Therefore God, addressing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, says: ﴿So let not their speech grieve you﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76]. Do not grieve, O Muhammad. Al-huzn (grief) is the soul's regret at not achieving what a person wishes and the occurrence of what corrupts. If the Messenger of God grieved and his soul was constricted, who would console him? Who would lighten it for him? The One who sent him consoles him, because He, glorified is He, counts everything against them and knows what they conceal and what they disclose.

﴿Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they disclose﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76].

But what is it that these people concealed?

Those who confronted the Messenger of God were of two kinds. One kind confronted him boldly, declaring with their tongues what was in their hearts, that they did not believe in him; these are the disbelievers (al-kafarah). The other kind professed belief with their tongues while concealing disbelief in their hearts; these are the hypocrites (al-munafiqun). So the meaning of ﴿what they conceal﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76] is hypocrisy, and ﴿what they disclose﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76] is disbelief. Or, ﴿what they conceal﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76] is their true belief in you, that you are a Messenger, trustworthy and truthful, and ﴿what they disclose﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76] is disbelief, as evidenced by the words of the Exalted: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [An-Naml: 14].

The evidence is that they did not deny the Qur'an, nor did they object to it. Their objection was rather that it should be sent down upon Muhammad in particular. Therefore they said, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 31].

And the evidence is that they used to entrust their deposits and trusts to the Messenger of God. All of this is proof of their belief in the Messenger of God. Yet, despite this, they proclaimed the word of disbelief out of fear for their temporal authority, their status, their lordship, and their tyranny, and the new religion came to strip them of all this and to end their domination over the weak and the poor.

Thus, they were bound to confront the Messenger of God and to stand against his call with all their strength, despite their inner conviction of his truthfulness. Therefore, in Madinah they were preparing to crown a king from among themselves, but when the Messenger of God entered it and the people gathered around him, their kingdom dissolved and vanished before it was born. The temporal powers that belonged to the disbelievers departed, just as authority departed from the hands of the Jews, who were people of knowledge, wealth, and warfare. All of this departed on the day the word of Islam became supreme.

Or: what is meant by ﴿what they conceal and what they disclose﴾ is that a person's action is the outcome of two matters: a thing or need that ferments in the soul, counted as a secret and a creed that drives him to action; if it is translated into action and comes out into existence, it becomes open. Accordingly, the meaning is: We know what they conceal of their corrupt beliefs, and what they disclose of the commission of abominations.

But would God boast of knowing a thing without benefit from that knowledge? The matter does not end with mere knowledge; rather, this knowledge must entail a recompense that punishes the disbelieving sinner and rewards the obedient believer. Therefore: consider your affairs, and beware of what follows from this knowledge of consequences, for the knowledge of God is not (fantaziyya) knowledge and awareness.

Therefore the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, honour belongs to God entirely﴾ [Yunus: 65]. Some understood that the phrase ﴿indeed, honour belongs to God entirely﴾ [Yunus: 65] is the speech of the disbelievers. But how could the disbeliever say it? Would that they had said it; rather, God said it as a concluding clause (tadhyil) to His words: ﴿And let not their speech grieve you﴾ [Yunus: 65]. Why? Because honour belongs entirely to God.

After the Exalted spoke of His signs in the horizons, on the earth, in the sun and the moon, the ship, the beasts and the cattle, He now speaks of His signs within the human soul, since if the signs in the horizons around them did not draw their attention to God, here are His signs in their own selves, which never leave them:

﴿Has man not considered that We created him from a drop of semen...?﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 36, verse 77:

His, the Glorified's, saying: ﴿Has man not seen﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77] means "knows," because man did not witness the process of creation within himself. If you say: who informed him, and who made him know that Allah is the Creator? They said: man recognized this truth, because in the universe there is a perfection that no one among the creatures has claimed. Then the world was startled by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informing that Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator, and no one opposed him. This, then, is a claim that has no opponent or challenger, although man often claims what does not belong to him. But this particular claim, no one can claim for himself.

The rule is that a claim is established for its owner so long as no opponent stands against it. Otherwise, if this claim were not granted to the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, then where is the Creator? Why did He not oppose it, and why did He not demand His right to creation? Either He shrank from confrontation, or He was not aware of this claim, and in both cases He does not deserve to be a god.

We note in the context of these verses that the Truth, the Glorified, said in the preceding verses: ﴿Have they not seen that We created for them, of what Our hands have done, cattle, so they are their owners?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71], and here He said: ﴿Has man not seen﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77], addressing man and not the group. They said: because this verse, or what is meant by "man" is man in general, so it is for every denier of resurrection who is of the likeness of Ubayy.

His, the Glorified's, saying: ﴿from a drop [nutfah]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77]. Empirical science has not reached anything in this matter of creation except recently, attempting shyly to uncover some secrets of human creation of what we did not know anything about before. The nutfah (sperm drop) is the essence and the microbe or the active germ that causes fertilization when it reaches the ovum, and this nutfah swims in a fluid which is the semen and lives in it. Therefore, the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 37].

Modern empirical science has established that the nutfah is responsible for determining maleness or femaleness, and the ovum is merely a container. Thus: the woman has no role in this matter, by the evidence of God's saying: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he was a clinging clot, then He created and proportioned, then made of him the two mates, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 37-39], that is, from the nutfah. And we said: it is remarkable that the Arab woman in ancient times perceived this truth which science did not arrive at except recently.

As for the Prophet's (ﷺ) hadith on this matter: they understood from this hadith that determining maleness or femaleness depends on the water that precedes. But when we reflect on the word itself, the word (ghalaba) indicates dominance and precedence, and precedence is only for elements that come out from one point and move in one direction. Therefore, the two are not opposed; the meaning of "yaghlibu" means "yasbiqu" (precedes).

We also said: they have now become aware that when the ovum comes out of the woman it causes a chemical change in the woman's constitution that causes a rise in body temperature, a change in mood and in heartbeats; therefore they invented a watch that measures these changes, by which the woman knows the time of the ovum's release.

The nutfah is a microbe extremely small, not seen except by microscope. May Allah have mercy on al-'Aqqad, who said a concise phrase depicting this smallness: he said that the offspring of the entire world, meaning the nutfahs that formed them, could be placed in half a sewing thimble. Glory be to the Creator who brings out from this extremely small nutfah a complete human being, and produces from it hard bones, semi-hard and soft muscles, and produces from it cartilage, nerves, liquid blood, and brain... etc.

This is in the material body, and more wondrous than it is what this body contains of intellect that understands, the tongue that speaks and tastes, the eye that sees, the hand that seizes, the nose that smells, the fingertips that touch, and the foot that walks.

All of these are from the nutfah, this microbe not seen by the naked eye, this nutfah which the Qur'an described as "mahin" water, "mahin" (despised) because man urinates it and it exits through the urinary passage, and is cast into toilets with filth, and if it touches your clothes it must be washed. And from this despised water man is created, and then he reaches the highest ranks of transgression and tyranny. How?

They said: because man has good qualities in his essence, and talents that he loves to display. If he is with his loved ones, he is pleased with his beautiful appearance, or his wealth, or his intelligence, etc., so he tries to show these talents to them. When he is confronted by enemies, he has other talents against his enemies, and with the enemy man mobilizes all his talents to triumph over his enemy: these are talents in anger, in dispute and in argument.

Therefore one of them said:

How many a blessing from Allah in me have I praised, gathered in me by three talents:
The first for myself, the second for my loved ones and companions, and the third for my adversary.

All of this is the meaning of ﴿then he is an open adversary﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77]. That is: after He created man from this nutfah and this despised water, we were surprised that he is ﴿a adversary [khasim]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77], meaning a fierce enemy, ﴿clear [mubin]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77], meaning he clearly expresses the talents of enmity within him with clear expression. A person is not clear to others unless the matter is clear within himself, because one who lacks a thing cannot give it. The failed teacher is the one who cannot convey information to his students, because the information is unclear to him; if the information were clear in his mind, he would be able to convey it by any method.

Thus: the meaning of ﴿mubin﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77] is one who excels in expressing what is in himself. Therefore you say: "abantu laka" (I made it clear to you) because it became clear to me, and "a'lamtuka" (I informed you) because it was known to me, and "afhamtuka" (I made you understand) because I understood; these are two talents, and man's talents rise and he mobilizes all his qualities in dispute, withholding nothing of them: in dispute he displays what he has of wealth, courage, or cunning, etc.

And it is wondrous that all of this lies dormant in the nutfah, and it is also wondrous that man transfers this dispute from his own self, and from his dispute with his enemies, to dispute with his Lord and Creator.

Therefore the Exalted said after it, depicting this dispute not with Ubayy, the occasion of revelation of the verses, but with everyone who is of Ubayy's likeness:

﴿And he struck for Us a parable and forgot his creation...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 36, verse 78:

We have spoken about the striking of a parable (ḍarb al-mathal), and we said: "ḍarb" means the impact of one body upon another with force. It is a condition that the one who strikes be stronger than the one struck; otherwise the result is reversed. Among this is the saying of al-Rafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him:

"Likewise, the striking of a parable is the bringing forth of something that falls upon something else, to show you its decisive and effective impact. When you doubt a thing, for example, he clarifies it for you with an example you do not doubt, bringing it close to your mind. Among this is the saying of the Exalted, when He wished to clarify for us the falsehood of polytheism and the difference between it and monotheism:

﴿Allah sets forth an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Zumar: 29].

Yes, a slave disputed over by several masters is not equal to a slave owned by one master. Likewise, monotheism and polytheism are not equal."

As for His saying, ﴿And he presents to Us a parable﴾, it means Ubayy ibn Khalaf. The parable he struck was that he took a bone that had decayed and began crumbling it in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "Do you claim, O Muhammad, that your Lord will bring this back to life after it has become what you see?" Although the verses were revealed concerning Ubayy, they are not restricted to him; rather they include every denier of resurrection who rejects this matter.

As for the meaning of ﴿and forgets his creation﴾, it means: if he were to remember his own creation and reflect on his own self, he would find the evidence against what he denies. For Allah created you from nothingness, so you came into existence. When you die, there remain from you these remnants which you crumble, scattered upon the earth. And it is known, according to what minds comprehend, that bringing something into existence from something existing is easier than bringing it into existence from nothing.

﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27].

In this verse, the Exalted addresses us according to the measure of our minds and in accordance with our reasoning. Otherwise, "easy" and "easier" would not be said of Him, the Exalted; such terms are said only of human beings.

Let us speak about the coining of parables (darb al-mathal). Darb means striking one body against another with force, and it is required that the striker be stronger than the struck. Otherwise the result is reversed. Among examples of this is the saying of al-Rafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him:

O you who mock at the turns of fate,
you are harming yourself, not fate.

O you who strike a rock with a staff,
did you strike the staff, or did you strike the rock?

Likewise, coining a parable (darb al-mathal) is bringing forth something that is set alongside something else, so as to show you its decisive and effective impact. When you doubt something, it clarifies it for you with an example you do not doubt, bringing it close to your mind. Among examples of this is the saying of Allah, the Exalted, when He wished to clarify for us the falsehood of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and the difference between it and tawhid (the oneness of Allah). He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Allah strikes a parable: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah, but most of them do not know.﴾ (Az-Zumar: 29).

Yes, a slave disputed over by several masters is not equal to a slave owned by one master. Likewise, tawhid and shirk are not equal.

As for His saying: ﴿And he coins for Us a parable﴾ (Ya-Sin: 78), that is, Ubayy ibn Khalaf. The parable he coined was that he took a bone that had decayed and began crumbling it before the Messenger of Allah, saying: "Do you claim, O Muhammad, that your Lord will bring this back to life after it has become what you see?" Although the verses were revealed concerning Ubayy, they are not restricted to him; rather they include every denier of resurrection (ba'th) who rejects this matter.

The meaning of ﴿and forgets his creation﴾ (Ya-Sin: 78) is: if he had remembered his own creation and reflected on his own self, he would have found the proof against what he denies. For Allah created you from nothingness, so you came to have existence. When you die, there remain from you these remnants which you are crumbling, scattered in the earth. It is known, according to what minds understand, that origination from something existing is easier than origination from nothing. ﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ (Ar-Rum: 27).

In this verse, the Real, glorified be He, addresses us according to the measure of our minds and in accordance with our logic. Otherwise, it would not be said of Him, the Exalted, that He is "easy" or "easier," or "simple" or "simpler." These are said only of human beings.

As for His saying: ﴿He says, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ (Ya-Sin: 78), when this question is put to the disbelievers who deny resurrection, they say: "No one can give life to the dead." Why? Because they measure the matter by the incapacity of power in human beings, not by the absolute power of the Creator, glorified be He.

What is remarkable is that Allah, the Exalted, ascribes the attribute of creating to man. He says: ﴿So blessed be Allah, the best of creators﴾ (Al-Mu'minun: 14), while man denies and rejects the power of Allah in creation. So if your Lord has not withheld from you the attribute of being a creator, then do not withhold from Him that He is the best of creators.

We have said: whenever you find an attribute of Allah that is also ascribed to human beings, you must understand it within the framework of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ (Ash-Shura: 11). Allah has a face, but not like faces; He has a hand, but not like hands; and so on. This is because Allah is one in His essence, one in His attributes, and one in His acts. Allah exists and you exist, but your existence is not like His existence. Allah is rich (ghani) and you are rich, but your richness is not like the richness of Allah. The richness of Allah is essential and inseparable from Him, glorified be He, whereas your richness is bestowed.

Allah is a creator and you are a creator, but there is a difference between your creating and the creating of Allah. Your creating is from something existing, whereas the creating of Allah, the Exalted, is from nothing. Your creation is inanimate and has no life in it, whereas the creation of Allah has life: it grows, nourishes itself, reproduces, and so on. So you are a creator, but your Lord, glorified be He, is the best of creators.

Therefore: Allah, the Exalted, possesses the attributes of absolute perfection, from which He bestows upon His creation, granting them some of His attributes, but absolute power remains His, glorified be He.

The meaning of ﴿rameem﴾ (Ya-Sin: 78) is: ancient, decayed, crumbling to pieces.

Then the Real, glorified be He, responds to this denier and his like: ﴿Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time﴾ (Ya-Sin: 79). The meaning of ﴿produced them﴾ is: from nothing, and to produce them from something existing is even more fitting. His saying ﴿the first time﴾ (Ya-Sin: 79), in the response to this denier, suggests that there is another time, and another giving of life different from the first. ﴿And He is Knowing of every creation﴾ (Ya-Sin: 79), that is: knowing of the first creation and of the second creation. Knowledge of the first creation is that He gives it attributes and capacities within its essence, makes it inhabit the earth, and provides it with a path that organizes its life there.

Through this path He guided it to the way of good, warned it against the ways of evil, and made clear to it the reward for this and that. He, glorified be He, is knowing of the other creation in the Hereafter, that is, He knows how to recompense it for what it has advanced. Therefore, the meaning of ﴿And He is Knowing of every creation﴾ (Ya-Sin: 79) is: He knows how to impose responsibility upon it, and He knows how to recompense it, and recompense corresponds to the measure of responsibility.

The Muslim philosophers wished to clarify this meaning for us, and they said: When Allah wanted to create from nothing, before the heaven or the earth existed, He said: "Come forth, O heaven, be heaven," and it was. Likewise the earth. Therefore, His capability, glorified be He, is what acted, and the createdness (maqduriyya) of things is what was acted upon. What, then, has ended from these two elements? They remain, both existing: the capability of the Agent, glorified be He, and the createdness of things.

Almighty God presents them with another proof of His absolute power. If you deny resurrection, then look at this material sign that you witness: the One who gives life to the bones that have crumbled to dust is the One who made for you fire from the green tree, which you kindle. The green branch catches fire, and greenness is a sign of moisture and water. How can fire come from water? This is a sign they see every day in Arab lands. It is well known that firewood is the first fuel man knew and used safely, because it is the purest fuel; it is healthy, does not pollute the environment, and does not harm it. You may compare firewood with petroleum fuel, for example, to see the difference.

This is a progression in the argument. Having mentioned the verse about God making green trees into fire, He then brings the stronger proof, the creation of the heavens and the earth. The heavens are a proof from a lofty, enduring height that does not change, and the earth is a proof close to us, which we see and handle. The occasion for this verse is found in another verse, where the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Certainly, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

If you say: "Explain to us how the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, even though they do not feel, speak, or know..." We say: Yes, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, because since God created them they have remained in their state and have not changed, and they will continue until the Hour arrives. As for you, O human, you die. You die as a child, and even as a fetus in your mother's womb. You die as a young man, and as an aged, decrepit elder. The most you can reach, even if you are granted a lifespan of a hundred years or a few years more, is limited. So where is your lifespan compared to the lifespan of the sun, the moon, or the earth? Have you ever seen a servant who lived longer than his master?

We come and go upon this universe as individuals, nations, and states. All of them depart and perish, while the heavens and the earth remain as they are, lofty and great. No change befalls them, and they never depart at all from the law of subjugation (qanun al-taskhir, the ordained law by which creation is made subservient to God's command). Since God created this universe, we have never seen a planet leave its orbit, fail to keep its appointed time, or refuse to carry out its task.

This is the condition of the inanimate things in the heavens and the earth. So what is your condition, O you who have intellect? If we speak of matter, it remains while you die. And in meanings and values, these inanimate things cooperate, while you oppose one another, disagree, and fight. So which of you, then, is better in creation and greater?

Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, answers this negated question: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?...﴾

Then He says: ﴿Yes﴾, that is, yes, He is able. ﴿And He is the Creator, the All-Knowing﴾. "Khallaq" is an intensive form of "khaliq" (creator), to affirm this matter for every denier of it. And He, glory be to Him, is the All-Knowing, that is, of those whom He created.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ Here is a subtle indication from the Truth, glorified is He, to every denier of the Resurrection, as if Allah were saying to them: O you who deny God's power to raise the bones that have crumbled to dust, do you suppose that Allah creates through treatment, as you create? The Creator does not create by treatment. Rather, He creates by the word "Be" (kun). In fact, He, glorified is He, creates merely by His will: if He wills a thing, it comes to be, without saying and without commanding. The word "Be" is only there to bring the matter closer to our minds.

We have already clarified this process with an example, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness. We said: How can you, O human being, deny God's power, when He has bestowed its like upon you in your own self? For example, when you wish to rise from your seat, what do you do? Did you command your muscles to move? Indeed, do you even know what the muscles are that lift you, and what the nerves are that control this process?

You rise merely by your will to rise, and you have no part in it. The evidence is that the small child, who knows nothing of how his body is formed, rises when he wishes to rise. If you, O human being, have things act for you without your saying to them, "Act," then is it fitting for you to deny this with regard to your Lord and Creator?

If you say: "Why then do I not command my limbs and say to them, 'Do such and such'?" We say: The Truth, glorified is He, says to a thing "Be" because He, glorified is He, knows that things will obey His command and will not depart from His will. Rather, are you certain that they will obey your command if you command them? You are not certain of this matter, as evidence by the fact that when Allah, exalted is He, takes away this power from a person, his limbs depart from his obedience: he wants to rise and cannot; the limbs become paralyzed and do not move.

So we say: If the created being's mere will controls his limbs, do we then find it unlikely that the will of the Supreme Creator controls this universe which was created for Him, glorified is He?

The word "Be" (kun) is said by Allah to bring our understanding of the matter closer, and He says it because things never fail to obey Him or respond to His command. As for you, if you say it, no one will hear you. Therefore He, glorified is He, said, explaining the earth's response to His command:

﴿And it has listened to its Lord and it was obligated﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 2], meaning: it was right for it to listen and to obey.

As for His saying "that He says to it" — meaning, to the thing that does not yet exist — how does He address it while it is still unseen? The scholars said: The Creator, glorified is He, created all things from eternity in a world called "the World of Images" (ʿālam al-mithāl). So things exist in actuality, but await the command to emerge and come forth into the world of existence. Therefore one of the knowers (ʿārifīn) said: "Matters that He manifests, and does not originate."

We learned in the previous verse that when Allah, glorified is He, says "Be!" things are affected and obey Him, whereas if a human says it, nothing responds to him. We also said that when an attribute of Allah is mentioned that is also used for humans, we must understand it within the framework of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. It is therefore fitting that these verses, and the whole surah, end with His saying, ﴿So glory be to Him in whose hand is the malakut (the hidden dominion, or unseen realm) of all things﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83]. That means: exalting Him above being resembled by anyone, whether in His essence, His attributes, or His acts.

The word ﴿malakut﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83] comes from the root m-l-k. This root is used in four meanings. The first is mālik (owner), which refers to anyone who possesses something, even a little. If he owns only the garment he wears, he is called a mālik. The second is malik (king), who has possession over those who are under his control, meaning he can dispose of them and direct their movements. The third is mulk (sovereignty), which is the rule over apparent matters that people know. The fourth is malakut, which refers to a hidden dominion that is not apparent. It is stronger and more comprehensive than mulk.

A thing may belong to the realm of malakut and then pass into the realm of mulk, like things that were unseen and then were discovered or invented by people, so they became witnessed. There are other things that remain always in the realm of malakut, and we know nothing about them except in the Hereafter. This is the kind that they deny. Among this is His saying concerning our master Ibrahim: ﴿And thus did We show Ibrahim the malakut of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 75].

Indeed, Allah makes him see the realm of malakut, because when He showed him the realm of mulk and tested him, he succeeded in the test with distinction. He succeeded in every stage of his life. He succeeded when he was an elderly man in the matter of sacrificing his son Isma'il, and he succeeded when he was thrown into the fire. Therefore he became worthy of Allah revealing to him the secrets of the universe and the realm of malakut. It is like when you have a righteous child in whom you see signs of excellence, so you single him out with something that favours him over the rest of your children. Likewise, whoever performs worship of Allah well, Allah grants him generously.

Among this is what the Qur'an narrates to us in Surat al-Kahf about the righteous servant whom the Prophet Musa accompanied and learned from. Allah said about him: ﴿So they found a servant of Our servants, to whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us﴾ [al-Kahf: 65]. This righteous servant was not a prophet, and revelation was not sent down to him, yet the Prophet learned from him. Why? Because he took what the Messenger brought and applied it to himself. When Allah knew from him that he could be trusted with His methods and His secrets, He increased him and gave him of His knowledge, the divinely bestowed knowledge (ladunni), and revealed to him some secrets of the malakut.

Do you not see that our master Musa, peace be upon him, became angry with him when he damaged the boat and deliberately made it defective, and it belonged to poor, needy people? This is the realm of mulk, which the righteous servant perceived. As for his knowledge of the realm of malakut, it is in His saying: ﴿And behind them was a king who seized every boat by force﴾ [al-Kahf: 79]. So Allah gave the righteous servant knowledge of part of the realm of malakut, just as He gave Ibrahim, peace be upon him, knowledge of the malakut of the heavens.

The word malakut (ملكوت) carries the meaning of intensification, like rahamut (great mercy), jabarut (great might), and rahabut (great awe). It is therefore an intensification of mulk. However, the scholars of the recitations (qira'at) note that one of them recites ﴿Master of the Day of Judgement﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4] as "Malik" (مَلِكِ) without the intensive form. They said this is because the discussion concerns the Day of Judgement, and on that day all sovereignty belongs to Allah, and no one has any sovereignty, not even over the garment he wears.

Similarly, we say in the adhan (call to prayer) "Allahu Akbar," where the attribute "akbar" is mentioned without intensification, and the name "al-Kabir" is not mentioned. How can this be in the emblem of prayer, which is the pillar of religion? We use the attribute rather than the name. They said: because the adhan calls people away from their works to respond to the call of their Lord, and work has its standing in Islam, since it is a person's task in life and through it he reaches obedience to Allah. Therefore religion values it and does not belittle it.

The meaning of "Allahu Akbar" is that work is great and important, but Allah is greater and the call of your Lord is more important. As for "Kabir," it is one of the names of Allah. The meaning of "Kabir" is that everything other than Him is small. Therefore, in the adhan, the attribute is used rather than the name.

So His saying, ﴿So glory be to Him in whose hand is the malakut of all things﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83], means: whatever you see and whatever you do not see of dominion, and what is hidden from you, which you then reach through knowledge and discover, and that which you do not see of dominion until Allah informs one of His servants of it: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved﴾ [al-Jinn: 26-27].

The truth is that the hidden matters and secrets buried in the universe are not discovered by a human; rather, they are revealed to him. We have said that every secret in the universe which Allah wishes to make manifest to him has a time and a moment of birth. If its moment of birth coincides with your search, it appears at your hands; otherwise Allah makes it appear to you by chance at its appointed time, even if you were not searching for it. Therefore they say that ninety-seven percent of life's discoveries appeared to us by chance.

He, glorified is He, says in the Verse of the Throne: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. A human encompasses only a little of Allah's knowledge, and he does not encompass even this little except by His knowledge and His permission, when He permits the birth and manifestation of a thing.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83], it means the Day of Resurrection. So be mindful of this truth. Whoever does not believe in the blessing of creation will be frightened by the blessing of the return and the final destination. You were not created in vain, nor will you be left aimless.
